Cafe Noir is perfectly located right next to Pizza 4P’s, tucked into the lively vibe of Indiranagar. We visited on a Saturday for dinner—while the indoor seating was quite full, the outdoor area was pleasantly calm (minus a few insects 🙃). The ambience overall is really inviting.

We tried their mocha frappe, which was pure bliss! Alongside that, the OG smash burger was absolutely delicious, and the prawn ravioli—wow! Easily one of the best I’ve had so far.

They also have a good selection of wine for those who enjoy it. Overall, it’s a great spot to check out if you’re in Indiranagar.

I don’t drink coffee, so this review is a mix of her coffee experience and my ambience-first perspective.

Starting with the coffee (purely based on my friend’s take):
She genuinely liked it. The coffee had a strong, distinct flavour and didn’t feel like the usual “generic café coffee.” You can tell they’ve actually worked on the brew, not just served something standard.

Coming to ambience and vibe—it’s good. Not crazy, not mind-blowing, but solid Indiranagar café energy. Clean, comfortable, well-located, and easy to chill at. If you’ve been around Indiranagar cafés a lot, this won’t shock you—but it also won’t disappoint.

Food & pricing:
Everything is on the pricier side, but honestly, that’s expected for an Indiranagar café. Nothing felt bad, just not something that makes you want to come back again and again.

Had a mixed experience at Anaia Cafe.

The pesto pasta and alfredo pasta were amazing - rich, flavourful, and perfectly cooked. The fries and garlic bread were also good.

The ambience was really nice, and service was good as well, which made the overall experience pleasant.

The only disappointment was the hot chocolate. It tasted more like Bournvita than actual hot chocolate.

The highlight of our visit was the cheesy butter garlic broccoli - so good that we ended up ordering it three times! Definitely a must-try.

Price-wise, it’s not exactly expensive, but the portions are quite small, which makes it feel a bit pricey for the quantity.

Overall, great taste and atmosphere - just wish the portion sizes were better.

Copper + Cloves is a beautiful, plant-based oasis in Bangalore that is perfect for escaping the city's chaotic traffic. The vibe is incredibly serene, filled with lush greenery and a fantastic collection of books if you want to spend a quiet day out with clean food.

The Hits: The coconut matcha and seasonal matcha were absolutely great. The breakfast plate was amazing, and the toasties were another big hit at our table.

The Miss: The vegan khabuska was just not for us. Three of us couldn't even finish half of it, but unfortunately, we still had to pay full price for it.

Overall, it is a lovely spot for wholesome food and a peaceful atmosphere, just be mindful of what you order!

text.text:
Copper Cloves Cafe goes straight into my Top 5 worldwide. No hesitation. No debate. Just straight up there.
Their motto says “Slow Down” and somehow the whole place actually listens. The atmosphere, inside and outside, is crafted with style and soul. Books everywhere. Flowers softening every corner. Shelves that invite you to browse. A cozy kids’ space. It feels curated, not decorated.
And the food… my oh my. An unbeatable all vegan menu, sourdough that deserves its own fan club, and flavors that are thoughtful, balanced and seriously delicious. Every dish tastes like someone cared deeply before it reached your table.
The staff? 100% service minded and genuinely kind. Professional, warm, smiling. The kind of team that makes you feel welcome without hovering.
And then the magic spreads. Right there you have Love Me Twice for thrift treasures, Champaca for books you suddenly cannot live without, and No Nasties + for conscious reuse finds. The café is nestled into this whole universe like the warm heart of it all.
People stay. They read. They work. They talk. Time stretches gently. It has that Hotel California feeling, you can check out but you never really leave.
Adorable. Inspiring. Delicious. I will absolutely be back.

text.text:
The place is spacious and looks inviting right from the outside. Once you walk in, you can choose between the upstairs and downstairs seating. We picked the upstairs section, which felt quite peaceful overall, although conversations from nearby tables were still very audible. Given the upscale pricing, I expected the tables to be spaced out a bit more.

The menu itself is quite interesting, with a lot of unique options. They also feature seasonal specials, including mango-based coffees, desserts, and baked items, and even jackfruit-inspired offerings.

Here’s what we ordered and what we thought:

Jackfruit Latte
It genuinely tastes like jackfruit because you can clearly tell they use real jackfruit purée. Unfortunately, the one we got leaned quite bitter and wasn’t particularly enjoyable for us. Maybe it would work better with added sugar, but we personally prefer our drinks without it.

Cold Coffee
This was really good. Nicely balanced and not overly sweet.

Korean Bun
Easily the highlight of our order. The bun tasted fresh, and the cream cheese filling was rich and enjoyable.

Piri Piri Fries
Pretty average overall. It didn’t really have the distinct piri piri flavour we expected.

Overall, the place has great vibes, an interesting menu, and enjoyable food.

Sitting right in the hustle and bustle of Indiranagar, The Kind is a one-of-a-kind comfort place for me.
The ambience wraps you up in a comforting hug with lighting that is neither scanty nor too bright. It's a place to sit with a friend, sip matcha, and catch up on things from a year ago. The waiters are the kindest, tending to your needs and wants with the best dishes.
Although I love one of the "boring" dishes: the Belgian chocolate smoothie bowl with extra almond toppings.
It's a place to sit, read, catch up, and get to know your date. Whatever may be the purpose, The Kind is the kind of answer you are looking for. It has become my regular now.

Tried out Paper & Pie and here’s the honest take—

The vibe is clean and nice—one of those places that makes you feel slightly more productive just by sitting there.

Coffee? Solid. Egg options? Actually pretty great. Sandwiches? Let’s just say they won’t be solving world hunger anytime soon. 😄
Cold coffee was a win though, and the pudding felt like it was trying to be healthy… and mostly succeeding.

Is this some mind-blowing, life-changing café? Nah. But that’s kind of the charm.

It’s a really good spot to sit down, get some work done, have a proper conversation with a friend, or even sneak in a meeting without it feeling like a corporate box.

Overall—good food, good coffee, clean vibe, zero drama. Not extraordinary, but reliably nice… and honestly, that’s sometimes exactly what you need.

text.text:
So here I am back in Bangalore with a scratched thigh and face. so I decided to go and relax in a very calm well lit cafe!
suggested from a friend she told me to try the cinnamon roll... sadly they were out!
so I decided to ask what they would recommend. I was put into a conversation with Jagdish, who was the manager. I asked him what he would recommend for a person who visits their cafe for the first time. He quickly pointed out
mizo caramel cappuccino (5/5) -
Not a big fan of coffee yet wanting to try something new I said go ahead get me one of those. it was just perfect... I didn't know I would like a cup of cappuccino so much. just a perfect blessing to my palette after a long tiring day. Surely my injuries would be healing faster as i sipped through the cappuccino.

He also recommended a dessert Vanilla choux bun (4/5)
it was a nice snack with a lot of cream and a nutty texture with a hint of Chocolate. not too sweet and not too dry for the mouth a perfect blend. I liked the powdered sugar on top but I would say that I wouldn't like that as a recommendation over the other more famous desserts I have heard from that place.

We also had the signature Hot chocolate ( 4/5)- the hot chocolate was good... but I like my hot chocolate less sweet and a little bit more creamy.

to finish our evening and have our stomachs filled for a long walk we had a
cream cheese bagel (4/5)
I liked the bagel it felt fresh toasted and the cheese cream as well. I loved the salads but I felt the dish was a little incomplete. would love to see the cafe experiment more and try to add something that compliments this dish more.

This is mostly a place i would like to visit during office meetings or with a date a silent vibe with a well lit environment and quite friendly staff.

I loved the venue (5/5) as it was well lit and was spacious didn't feel cramped up.
I loved the hygiene (5/5) and simplicity yet unique vibe the place carried.
I loved the food (4/5), the easy to munch and have place for more deserts.

my recommendation for the place would just to find something to partner with or complete some of the dishes which I tried and i would love to visit here again soon!

Thank you Jagdish and all the servers who helped me find a new brew to keep my evenings jolly!

The main advantage of their space is that, it is well spread out. Which means that two tables are not placed very close to each other. Decent food menu for a coffee shop. The veggies pizza was good, in terms of taste and size.
Area of improvement : They are a multi-storey café, and the dessert tower is located on the ground floor only, which is fine. But they should atleast have a dessert menu available to everyone, irrespective of which floor they are sitting on. When I spoke to server, I understood that, they expect guests to climb down stairs each time they want to make a dessert selection. That is impractical. And even if we asked the server as to what all are available today, they wouldn't know anything, and would ask us to climb down stairs just to take a look at the dessert tower. And only then the dessert order would be taken.
Let's assume, the dessert menu chnages on regular basis, so they should have a backup plan of temporary/manual menus, just for dessert part. This is the least the team could do. Not everyone would know where what is placed in the first visit itself. And even if it is a repeat visit, one may not remember.
This experience was silly and a big shortcoming from the Conçu team's end.

Casa Fresco in Indiranagar is a total gem! Nestled under a leafy canopy with a charming brick facade, it’s the perfect "All Day Dining" retreat. The vibe is 5/5—peaceful, aesthetic, and quintessential Bengaluru.
The vegetarian spread we had was impressive. The Honey Chilli Sesame Fries were a highlight, perfectly glazed and crunchy. For a richer bite, the Creamy Mushroom Bruschetta is a must-try. We also loved the Pink Sauce Pasta and the Fried Paneer Popcorn, which were fresh and flavorful. From the crispy appetizers to the cozy breakfast omelettes, everything was spot on. A perfect spot for brunch or a quiet work afternoon!
Rating: 5/5

text.text:
We visited the Hole in the Wall Cafe, Indiranagar branch, over the weekend and had a pleasant overall experience, though it didn't quite stand out enough to justify the long wait.

For food, we ordered the chicken sandwich, Farmer's Pie, and a couple of drinks. The chicken sandwich was well-made, with fresh ingredients and a good balance of flavors. It was simple, satisfying, and exactly what you'd expect from a café known for its comfort food.

The highlight of the meal was definitely the Farmer's Pie. It came with generous chunks of chicken that were tender and flavorful, paired with a substantial portion of creamy mashed potatoes. The mashed potatoes complemented the chicken really well, making it a hearty and comforting dish that felt worth ordering.

The drinks were refreshing and paired nicely with the meal, though they weren't particularly memorable compared to the food.

Service was decent despite the weekend rush. The staff were courteous and managed the crowd reasonably well. However, the waiting time was quite long, which affected the overall experience. While the food was enjoyable, it wasn't exceptional enough to make the wait feel worthwhile. In an area like Indiranagar, where there are numerous cafes and brunch spots offering equally good food with shorter waiting times, it's difficult to see this as the obvious choice.

Overall, it's a good café with comforting food, especially the Farmer's Pie, but if you're visiting during peak hours, be prepared for a wait. Worth trying once, but there are plenty of other strong options in the neighborhood that offer a similar experience.

text.text:
The Hole In The Wall is one of those breakfast spots that lives up to the hype. Their English breakfast is genuinely satisfying—well-portioned, flavorful, and consistently good. From eggs and toast to sausages and sides, everything feels comforting and well done. The café has a warm old-world charm, with homely interiors that feel somewhere between a bookstore and a library, making it a lovely place to sit and slow down.

The only downside is the wait. There’s usually a long queue, and getting a table can mean waiting one to two hours since they don’t take prior reservations—you have to show up, take a token, and wait for your name to be called. Parking is another challenge, as there’s hardly space and vehicles often end up lined along the road outside.

The café has a warm old-world charm, with homely interiors that feel somewhere between a bookstore and a library, making it a lovely place to sit and slow down.

text.text:
Vanamo is hands-down one of the finest fine-dine cafés in Bangalore, tucked away in the vibrant streets of Indiranagar. From the moment we stepped in, we were welcomed into a space that strikes the perfect balance between elegance and comfort. The interiors are chic, the vibe is warm, and the attention to detail—in both décor and dishes—is clearly top-notch.

What sets Vanamo apart is its carefully curated global menu that leans into different Asian and European cuisines. Though the options may seem limited at first glance, each dish is crafted with intention, authenticity, and finesse. Presentation is beautiful, portions are satisfying, and the taste is refined—easily meeting European standards.

A huge shoutout to Nandhu, whose friendly demeanor and attentive service made our dining experience even more memorable. The staff overall was courteous and patient, adding to the feel-good experience.

What We Ordered:
- Patatas Bravas
A Spanish favourite—crispy double-cooked smashed potatoes laid on a vibrant, spicy bell pepper bravas sauce, chimichurri, and topped with sour cream. Crunchy, flavourful and beautifully plated.

- Mexican Fajita Burrito Bowl
A hearty, well-balanced bowl of chipotle-glazed cottage cheese, Mexican rice, refried beans, and sautéed bell peppers, paired with tortilla chips, guacamole, salsa and smoked sour cream. Comfort food at its best with an elevated twist.

- Hot Café Mocha
A warm hug in a cup—silky espresso with steamed milk and just the right amount of indulgent chocolate.

- Peach and Jalapeño Shock
A refreshing mocktail combining the sweetness of peach and orange juice with the gentle heat of jalapeño, finished with sparkling water. Unexpected, exciting and absolutely worth trying.

Vanamo may be on the premium side price-wise, but it delivers on every front—ambience, service, taste, and presentation. It's perfect for date nights, special occasions, or when you just want to treat yourself to a thoughtfully curated global menu in the heart of Bangalore.

text.text: The one word that comes to mind with Huvu is basic and not in a bad way. I loved how normal this place is. With so many cafes opening up around town competing for the best matcha, decor, hospitality, a place like Huvu just makes sense sometimes. It gives you that calm posture with its all white vibe along with open space. It sits at the corner of a busy intersection but you don't seem to feel the cocktail of pollution that usually hits you while you walk around town. Being on an elevated floor helps too. The coconut shake was great. No complaints on the mushroom omlettes. It's a home made sort of feel to everything. Work friendly with a dedicated balcony for smokers too. I could see myself coming here often to maybe read a book or catch up on some show. It sure beats the sulking on the couch all afternoon.

The staff were friendly and the ambience was typical of a cute cafe. They didn’t have an elevator though and finding parking on the street was a bit of a pain. Overall, we had an amazing breakfast and it made our day. Would love to visit back again.

I recently visited TrueBrew Café & Restaurant in Indiranagar and had a wonderful experience. The ambience is cozy and welcoming, making it a perfect spot for both casual dining and coffee catch-ups.

The highlight of my visit was the brewing expertise of Chang, who truly deserves appreciation for his excellence. With over 8+ years of experience in brewing, Chang has mastered the craft of creating perfectly balanced coffees. The cappuccino I tried was rich, aromatic, and brewed with precision—one of the best I’ve had in Bangalore.

The food was equally impressive. The Mazze Platter was well presented and flavorful, the Lemon Cake Slice was ok ok and the Cold Coffee was refreshing. Service was prompt and courteous, and the staff made sure we were comfortable throughout.

Overall, TrueBrew Café not only serves delicious food and beverages but also stands out because of passionate people like Chang who elevate the whole experience. Definitely worth visiting if you’re around Indiranagar!

Visited on a December morning in 2025. The amazing smell of coffee once you enter is so welcoming!!

We came here after some light breakfast. Ordered the Eggs Florentine on the Sourdough bread which was superb. The egg was just runny, the sourdough slice and some spinach was a lovely taste. It was a very well made Sandwich.

The Veg Croissant sandwich was good too. The cheese was cool and nice and sandwich was just flaky while still holding on to the goodies inside very well. Quite filling.

We ordered a Malabar brew Latte and a Kenyan brew latte. Both were good and distinct in taste.

As a cafe service can be laid back for the food, but the coffees do come pronto. Clean washroom and hand wash.  The price is on the above average / higher side but you do pay for the quality.

Parking on the street is tough , we had parked about a km away and taken a rickshaw. Am sure one can find parking in one of the back roads if you get in early. Place is quite popular and was filling up by about 12:30.

We came here for the specialty coffee that they claim to serve but they absolutely do not serve any specialty coffee, cold brew, or pour over whatsoever.

When I requested the specialty coffee they gave me a weak, filtered coffee, and they have the arrogance to think I can’t tell the difference. When I challenged them on this, they said it was a pour over that they did at the counter, I couldn’t see it as we were seated outside. When they offered to change it, they came back with another filtered coffee, insisting it was a pour over. When I went inside to pay the bill, there was no sign of a V60 or pour over equipment.

Not only this, the cappuccino that my wife ordered wasn’t professionally made as the milk and foam was thin, indicating they may not have trained baristas. Plus, the food was poor. The scrambled eggs was the worst I’ve had in Bangalore, and the sausages were the cheap, hot dog type you get in a tin, which are highly carcinogenic. text.text:
Some places serve great food, but a few serve a story with it - and Mon Chéri is one of them.
Learning that this restaurant was born from a mother's love, simply because her daughter loved Italian food, made the experience even more meaningful. It's beautiful to see how that love and passion have grown into a place where so many people can enjoy authentic, heartwarming Italian cuisine.

Every dish reflected care, freshness, and attention to detail. Beyond the food, the warm conversation with the owner ma'am and her daughter was the highlight of our visit. Their kindness, humility, and genuine passion made us feel less like customers and more like welcomed guests.

Thank you for sharing not just wonderful food, but a truly inspiring story. Wishing Mon Chéri many more years of success and countless happy diners. We'll definitely be back. ❤️

Overall- 4/5
In dine service- 4.5/5

1. Mushroom basque soup- 5/5. This soup was damn delicious! The mushrooms with the earthy umami taste and a hint of pepper that lingers till the next dish arrives. The spice is not overpowering.

2. Pasta (spaghetti) - 3.5/5. It was okay. The thin spaghetti & the cremey cheese sauce with chicken was not anything out of the ordinary or over the moon.

3. Fish & chips- 4/5. It was good. The fish was fresh, and the batter was crispy. We were given 2 portions of fish. The wedges were fresh, crispy & to the point. The tartar sauce was a perfect compliment to the fish & chips.  Would be nice to have vinegar to top the fish with.

4. Tipsy tiramisu-5/5. It was light & airy, not too sweet, with a tinge of bitterness. I would definitely have this again.

Portions- good & value of money. Can be shared. We shared our order between 3 people.

No wheelchair accessibility. Only staircase.♿❌

✅Reserve the table beforehand!!

Mon Cheri Crafted Continental Dining – A Delightful Culinary Experience in Indiranagar

Our visit to Mon Cheri was a last-minute plan, and we were lucky enough to get a table within 10 minutes. That said, I would highly recommend making a reservation in advance, as there were quite a few people waiting for a long time. And honestly, that itself tells a story about the popularity of this place.

Located in the heart of Indiranagar, the restaurant has a warm and well-maintained ambience that makes for a pleasant dining experience. If you're driving, it's better to park on one of the parallel roads nearby, as parking can be a bit challenging around the restaurant.

Coming to the food—the highlight of the experience. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, with quality ingredients and great flavors. I don't quite remember the names of everything we ordered, but I've shared the photos, and they speak for themselves! The presentation was excellent, and each dish was delicious in its own way.

Overall, Mon Cheri offers a wonderful combination of good food, inviting ambience, and attentive service. A lovely place for a relaxed meal with friends or family, and definitely worth a visit if you're in Indiranagar.

Rameshwaram Cafe is famous for its delicious, authentic, ghee-laden South Indian food (especially dosas & filter coffee), exceptional hygiene, fast service, strong social media buzz, and a unique "no refrigeration, no preservatives" policy, creating fresh, flavorful, and Instagrammable dishes that attract massive crowds and influencer attention, making it a modern South Indian food icon in Bangalore.
Key reasons for its fame:

Authentic & Fresh Flavors: Focuses on traditional recipes, quality ingredients, and serving food immediately without refrigeration or artificial additives, giving it a unique taste.

Signature Dishes: Famous for its rich, buttery ghee dosas (especially the Podi Masala Dosa) and aromatic filter coffee.

Hygiene & Quality: Strict hygiene standards and founder control over operations ensure consistent quality across outlets.
Social Media & Marketing: Masterful use of social media, creating visually appealing food and spaces that encourage user-generated content, turning customers into marketers.

Consistency: Delivers a reliable taste and experience, even with high volumes, building trust.

Fast Service Model: A quick-service format with high turnover, designed for busy city dwellers.

Entrepreneurial Success: Rapid growth from a small outlet to a major brand, attracting attention as a startup success story.

text.text:
recently visited Smoor Lounge, and it was truly a wonderful experience from start to finish. The place has such a peaceful, elegant, and cozy ambience, making it a perfect spot to relax and spend quality time with your partner. The calm atmosphere, comfortable seating, and soothing vibe make it ideal for meaningful conversations and unwinding from a busy day.
Coming to the food and desserts—absolutely amazing!
I tried a variety of items, and each one was delightful in its own way.
The Blueberry Cheesecake Pastry was rich, creamy, and perfectly balanced with just the right amount of sweetness. It felt fresh and indulgent, melting in the mouth with every bite.
The Pine Coco Craze Pastry was another highlight—unique, flavorful, and incredibly delicious. The combination of pineapple and coconut was refreshing and tropical, making it stand out from regular pastries.
For beverages, the Regal Rose was refreshing and soothing, while the Bubble Bubblegum drink was fun, vibrant, and surprisingly enjoyable—perfect if you like something playful and different.
The Cajun Spiced Fries were crispy, well-seasoned, and addictive. They were the perfect savory snack to balance out the sweetness of the desserts.
Overall, everything we ordered was fresh, well-presented, and full of flavor. The staff was polite and attentive, and the service was smooth and pleasant, which made the experience even better.
Smoor Lounge is truly a great place for dessert lovers and anyone looking for a calm, romantic, and classy environment. I would highly recommend it to couples, friends, or anyone who wants to enjoy premium desserts in a peaceful setting. I’ll definitely be visiting again! 🍰☕💖

text.text:
Tried Yogisthaan Cafe recently and honestly it was a disappointing experience.

The food was average at best and definitely overpriced for the quality they serve. I ordered a pasta and it felt like it was cooked in tons of tomato puree, completely overpowering the dish. It didn’t taste balanced at all.

The frappe with milk was another letdown. It literally tasted like the kind of milk you get from a milkman who mixes 70% water and 30% milk — extremely diluted and lacking any real flavor.

We also ordered sabudana khichdi, which was served with salted curd. When we asked if they could provide sweetened curd instead, they simply refused. Small requests like that shouldn’t be such a big deal for a cafe.

To make things even more confusing, the hash brown potato was served with curd. I mean… what? That combination just didn’t make sense.

On top of all this, there’s practically no parking space, which makes visiting the place quite inconvenient in a busy area.

Overall, it felt like a very average cafe that’s surviving mainly because it’s located in urban Bangalore, not because of the food quality or experience.

For the prices they charge, the food and overall experience were definitely disappointing.

Everything…and I mean EVERYTHING at this this breakfast spot is “melt in your mouth” delicious 🤤
I personally never knew idli could taste this good!
So a new favorite of mine is their Ghee Podi Thatte Idli. Its 100% worth the hype!
My hubby , mama & I also really enjoyed the ghee masala dosa and jaggery filter coffee. The aloo & onions plus the masala was just the perfect combination. Honestly, the best masala I’ve had on a dosa before. The dosa also had a very nice crisp to it.

Another reason I love Srirangam Cafe is because of their hygiene. The tables are cleaned quickly and ready to serve the next customers and they even have a hand washing station to the left of the kitchen.

P.S. Just note there is no washroom available at the cafe, so all you need to do is head to a nearby coffee shop.

I recently visited Chai Days and had a very disappointing experience.

I ordered a Vietnamese iced coffee, but what I received was a small glass filled almost entirely with ice. The actual coffee quantity was so little that it was finished in just 2 sips. It honestly felt like I was paying for ice, not coffee.

When I raised this with the staff, they casually mentioned that this is how the owner has instructed them to serve it — essentially prioritizing ice over the actual drink. That’s not just poor service, it feels misleading and unfair to customers.

This kind of practice comes across as cutting corners at the expense of customer experience. Definitely not worth the price, and I wouldn’t recommend ordering iced beverages here.

text.text:
Started with hot chocolate, which was slightly diluted and only politely sweet. More of a warm cocoa-flavored beverage than a hug in a cup ☕😌

Then came the Nutella French toast wch was a absolute showstopper. Perfect Nutella ratio, sweetness on point, and the toast texture was chef-level good. Kiwi and strawberry on top made it look fancy without trying too hard. This one understood the assignment completely 🍓🍫

The Green Goddess sandwich looked heavy enough to question our life choices, but turned out surprisingly light and very tasty once eaten. A visual lie, but a pleasant one 🥪✨

French fries, unfortunately, were swimming in oil and still managed to have very little taste. A rare talent, honestly 🍟🫠

Avocado tahini sourdough sandwich was another win , well-balanced flavors with pomegranate and lettuce adding the right freshness. Clean, light, and satisfying.

Overall, a mix of stars and fillers. Come for the sandwiches and French toast, skip the fries, and don’t expect miracles from the hot chocolate.

text.text:
A Wonderful Experience at The Comedy Theatre, Indiranagar – Where Food, Coffee, and Laughter Meet
The Comedy Theatre in Indiranagar, Bangalore is truly a hidden gem that perfectly blends great food, comforting coffee, and a lively ambience with the magic of stand-up comedy. From the moment I walked in, I felt welcomed by the cozy interiors, warm lighting, and neatly arranged seating that gives the place a premium yet relaxed café-theatre vibe.
The cleanliness of the café deserves special appreciation. Every corner, from the dining tables to the floor and restrooms, was well maintained, which instantly gives confidence in the overall quality and hygiene standards. The atmosphere feels calm and elegant, making it a perfect place to spend time with friends, family, or even alone.
Coming to the food — it was absolutely delightful. The creamy white sauce pasta was rich, smooth, and perfectly cooked, topped with olives and served with a crispy garlic bread that complemented it beautifully. The seasoned fries with dip were crispy, flavorful, and addictive. The main course platter with rice, grilled vegetables, soft bread, and chicken in brown sauce was filling and well-balanced in taste. Every dish was well presented and tasted fresh and comforting. The Spanish Latte was smooth and aromatic, while the ferraro rocha chocolate drink was thick, rich, and satisfying — perfect for coffee lovers.
What truly elevated the experience was the hospitality of the staff. The team was polite, attentive, and genuinely caring. Though I slightly forgot the name, I believe it was Henry who assisted us — he was extremely courteous, friendly, and professional. His warm approach made the experience even more pleasant and personal.
The comedy stage setup, seating arrangement, and lighting create a fantastic environment for live performances.The performance starts at 9 pr 10 pm .It’s not just a café, it’s an experience — laughter, comfort, taste, and hospitality all in one place.
Overall, The Comedy Theatre is a must-visit in Indiranagar for anyone who loves good food, quality coffee, clean ambience, friendly service, and a joyful atmosphere. I would highly recommend this place and will definitely be visiting again.

Veg-friendly options: Loved the hummus samosa and broccoli soup – plenty for vegetarians like me.

Value spot: Affordable prices for such quality; ideal for brunch or quick grabs.

If you're in Bangalore, skip the chains and head to Glen's – you'll be hooked! Highly recommend

Glen's Bakehouse definitely has a lovely, rustic, and cozy ambiance—it’s a great spot if you just want to sit, relax, and catch up with friends. However, the food itself was pretty average and didn't quite live up to the hype.
We tried a few of their baked goods and savory items. While their signature mini red velvet cupcakes are decent, some of the other pastries felt a bit dry and lacking in freshness. The savory dishes (like the sandwiches/pizzas) were standard cafe fare—not terrible, but definitely not exceptional for the price you pay.
The service was alright, though slightly slow since the place tends to get quite crowded.
Overall, it's a nice place for the aesthetics and a basic cup of coffee, but if you are going purely for top-tier bakery items or a memorable meal, you might find it a bit underwhelming.

text.text:
A True South Indian Delight at The Filter Coffee, Indiranagar! ✨☕

Recently visited The Filter Coffee and it turned out to be an absolutely wonderful experience.

From the moment I stepped in, the warm hospitality and charming South Indian ambiance created a welcoming and relaxing atmosphere. The place beautifully blends simplicity, tradition, and comfort.

The highlight, of course, was the authentic filter coffee—rich, aromatic, perfectly brewed, and served at the ideal temperature. Every sip carried the nostalgic taste of traditional homemade South Indian coffee: bold, smooth, and incredibly satisfying.

The food was equally exceptional. The dosas were crisp and golden, the Pattani Vada was perfectly crunchy, and the chutneys and sambar were fresh, flavorful, and comforting. I also tried:
🥥 Seasoned Steam Balls – soft, fluffy, and surprisingly addictive
🍜 Idiyappam with Coconut Milk & Kurma
🍛 Vegetable Biryani
🥣 Sambar Rice Combo with Raita

Every dish was thoughtfully prepared, hygienic, and packed with authentic flavors that celebrate South Indian cuisine.

If you’re a fan of traditional South Indian food and a perfect cup of filter coffee, this place deserves a spot on your must-visit list.

The place is a lovely little joint on 80 Feet Road in Bangalore. We visited the restaurant for breakfast, and I was genuinely amazed by both the service and the food quality. To begin with, they serve everything on fresh plantain leaves — such a simple touch, but it adds so much charm to the experience.

Once you decide on the menu, the staff take care of everything with ease and efficiency. We ordered Idli, Mini Idlis, Vada, Dosa, and topped it all off with a classic filter coffee. Every item was served hot, fresh, and truly delicious.

A special mention must go to the accompaniments — the White Chutney, Red Chutney, and Sambar were all wonderful. The White Chutney, especially, was absolutely mind-blowing! As a foodie, I’m yet to taste anything quite like it. The coffee too was piping hot and perfectly brewed.

They also have a small confectionery and sweet shop attached, which makes the place even more delightful.

Overall good experience with the food and staff.

Truffles is a great spot for an affordable and satisfying meal. We ordered the Double Cheese Mushroom Burger, All American Veg Burger, Irish Coffee Shake, and a Green Apple Granita for two, and the total came to around ₹830, which felt very reasonable for the quantity and quality.

The All American Veg Burger with the double patty was definitely the showstopper loaded with cheese and perfect for cheese lovers. The Double Cheese Mushroom Burger was equally filling, and both burgers were served with chips and sauces on the side. The shakes and drinks were refreshing too.

Dessert wise, their apple pie is a must-try. However, I’m personally not a big fan of their lasagna.

The location is easy to reach from the metro, service is good, and the staff is polite. It does get quite crowded on weekends, with a wait time of around 15–20 minutes depending on the rush.

Overall, a perfect place for brunch or a casual meal with friends.

text.text:
Toit in Indiranagar is universally famous for its incredible craft beers, lively crowds, and fantastic night-out atmosphere, but if you haven’t visited them on a weekend morning for breakfast, you are genuinely missing out on one of Bangalore's best-kept secrets. Stepping into the familiar, beautiful wood-paneled space when it’s calm, flooded with morning sunlight, and smelling of fresh coffee instead of hops is an experience in itself. While their continental breakfast options look great, the absolute star of the morning is their stellar appam menu. I managed to try all their appam variations, and calling them heavenly is an understatement.

The kitchen handles traditional Kerala-style textures flawlessly. Every single version features perfectly made lacy appams brilliantly crisp, golden, and webbed at the edges, while remaining soft, pillowy, and beautifully cloud-like right in the center. The Bull’s Eye Appams are an absolute work of art, topped with flawless sunny-side-up eggs that break into a rich yolk, perfectly balanced by the sharp, savory bite of the accompanying Sri Lankan coconut sambal and podis. The Egg Roast and Appams hit with a comforting, nostalgic heat; the country eggs are enveloped in a deeply caramelized, intensely spiced tomato and onion masala that coats the delicate appams beautifully. Finally, the Appams with Stew offer pure, unadulterated comfort. The rich, velvety coconut milk base is subtly aromatic, perfectly infusing the fresh vegetables or meats, creating a mild yet complex flavor profile that cleanses the palate. Pairing these traditional, fiery, and comforting dishes with a hot South Indian filter coffee in a microbrewery setting is the ultimate weekend plot twist. It’s a phenomenal breakfast that deserves just as much fame as their beers.

As a beer lover, I never miss a visit to Toit whenever I’m in town, and this time too, it did not disappoint. Visited on a Wednesday evening with colleagues and had an okay overall experience.

Pros:

1. Absolutely loved their wide range of craft beers. The IPA and Hefeweizen were my personal favourites.
2. The food was equally impressive — freshly prepared, tasty, and served in generous portions.
3. The ambience has a rustic, woody charm that gives the place a warm and welcoming old-school vibe. The pub was also neat and well-maintained.
4. Compared to many other pubs, the pricing felt quite reasonable for the quality and experience offered.

Cons:

1. We had to wait for over an hour to get seated as there was a huge queue, and the staff seemed overwhelmed.
2. The service was quite slow. It took us more than 20 minutes just to get hold of someone to place our order, and the food arrived after another 35+ minutes.

Despite the delays, the beer, food, and ambience made the visit worthwhile.

text.text:
My first visit to Chaipatty was excellent. The owner was very friendly, and my friend and I worked from the café for around 4 hours. We ordered food worth more than ₹700, and I also paid separately for Wi-Fi, which was charged at ₹60 per hour. During that time, the owner even allowed me to use one of the rooms for a meeting. I was genuinely grateful for the support and hospitality. Before we left, the owner mentioned that many people come there to work and that they would be happy to host us again.

Because of that positive experience, I decided to return a couple of days later. If I had written my review immediately after my first visit, it would have been an easy 5-star rating.

However, my second visit was completely different. When I arrived, the café was almost empty. I worked there for about 3 hours and ordered food worth over ₹300. This time, I didn't use the Wi-Fi or even plug in my charger. After a few hours, the owner approached me and said the table was reserved. I was happy to move to another table, but then she commented that I had been sitting there without ordering anything. I offered to place another order, but the interaction made me feel unwelcome.

I packed up my things and left. What disappointed me most was the contrast between the warm welcome during my first visit and how I was treated on my second. I've worked from many cafés in Indiranagar and have never had an experience that made me feel this embarrassed or uncomfortable.

I understand that cafés need to manage seating and reservations, but clearer communication and consistency would have made a big difference. The reason I returned was because I genuinely believed what I was told during my first visit—that the café welcomed people who came to work. Unfortunately, my second experience left me feeling otherwise.

text.text:
Had dinner at Yuki recently. It was over-all a good experience. Following is what I ordered and my personal ratings:

1) Oriental Chicken Satay (8 out of 10): I personally found the chicken to be well flavoured, marinated and really juicy (although being chicken breast). I found the accompanying sause extremely sweet almost dessert like, but the Satay by itself is a must try.

2) Spicy Chicken and Celery Dimsum (7.7 out of 10): Honestly nothing to brag about, but a nice soup dumpling, and in a way really refreshing.

3) Belgian Pork Spare Ribs (7.8 out of 10): I found the pork to be slightly on the gamey-er side, but I enjoyed the tangy-sweet tamarind and chilli sause.

4) Spicy Miso Ramen Pork (7.2 out of 10): I liked pretty much everything about this dish, expect the noodles. I'm not sure what kind of noodles they used, but it didn't taste like the highest quality. I personally feel noodle holds the ramen together, hence I found this dish capable on a much needed improvement. I would strongly recommend a thinner noodle.

On the negative side, I found my table to pretty be sticky, likely from a beverage spill, which wasn't cleaned very well. I think Yuki can do better here to improve the dining experience.

The service was great, the staff were attentive, helpful and enthusiastic which added very positively to my dinning experience.

Something worth noting is that the restaurant can get loud, especially during the evenings, which can be unpleasant for a date or a smaller crowd, but that should be expected considering that it is also a cocktail bar.

text.text:
Located on the banks of indira nagar and thippasandra is a unique three floored socials like you have never seen before. Each floor has a theme of their own with the top floor turning into a rave party for the local DJs on a weekend night. The second floor is more of a quite zone and could be for those on date night. The bottom floor has a small dance floor as well. It definitely feels cramped up.

I like to get the negatives out of the way and that came in the form of their service. First of all they either need to keep the soft menus or remove them because we end up ordering from the phone which does not have all the items based on the time of the day. Even if you find a dish on the physical menu, it is so hard to locate that on the mobile app. They really need to improve on the UX of the application. The waiter also had no clue on the availability of certain dishes too. When we asked him to add those dishes through his system, he struggled and mentioned that the wifi was weak where we were sitting so was not able to place the order. Eventually he was able to. We waited for about close to 30-40 mins before we could place an order. Well that wasnt the end of the negatives. The ground floor AC unit was not working. I could have taken it on any other day but it being a Friday with an event going on, there was a flock of people which made the whole experience unbearable as well as suffocating. When we asked the staff, they mentioned that the unit was not working for the past 2 days. Not acceptable at all!!! I was just glad to be out of there.

Ok now thats done, its time for the positives which means its about the food. Socials everywhere has a standard when it comes to the food they serve. We had the mutton pressure cooker where they actually served it in a pressure cooker. We felt like taking the cooker home hahah. It was rich in flavor that was complemented with the spiciness. This made for the opening of a few sweat glands. The mixed grill platter was great as well. All the meat were cooked to perfection. Overall loved the food, not so much the rest of the package. Socials please look into these aspects. I feel the menu issue is something that the team might want to talk about. Either keep the physical menu or remove it. We end up wasting time because while deciding we were choosing dishes that were not available on the app.

Would absolutely visit again and bring other people.

text.text:
Landed in Bangalore and headed straight to Nerlu. Told the barista, Razi, that I wanted an iced black coffee and asked for a recommendation. He suggested the Citrus Cold Brew. I said, “Fair enough, let’s do it.”

Best decision of the day.

That Citrus Cold Brew was an easy 5 out of 5. Actually, scratch that. It deserves its own rating system. Easily the best cold brew I’ve had. Smooth, refreshing, ridiculously well balanced. One sip in and I was questioning every cold brew I’ve had before this. Absolute god tier stuff.

While we were busy discussing coffee, pour overs and other coffee nerd topics, Razi asked what roast profile I usually prefer. I said light roast. A few minutes later he handed me an iced pour over and told me to give it a try.

That was another winner. Clean, bright and exactly the kind of coffee that reminds you why people become coffee snobs in the first place.

After I finished both drinks, I went back to tell him how much I loved them. That’s when he told me the beans were from Beachville Coffee Roasters.

Naturally, I smiled and said, “Yeah, I know them.” Sometimes being a coffee nerd actually pays off.

Nerlu absolutely nailed the experience. Great coffee, great recommendations and even better conversations. If you’re in Bangalore and remotely interested in specialty coffee, just go. Don’t overthink it. The Citrus Cold Brew alone is worth the trip

text.text: Plan B in Indiranagar has become a fairly well-known casual dining spot in Bangalore’s East, often praised online for its lively ambience and relaxed vibe. But on our visit, the experience felt like a classic case of “good on paper, average in practice.” We started with a round of mocktails, but were struck by how inconsistent they were: every time we ordered a repeat, they arrived in different glasses and looked entirely different in presentation and colour. Unfortunately, this inconsistency was mirrored in taste and portion size too — which felt overpriced for what we got. The French fries variations we tried were solid and enjoyable, crisp and well-seasoned, but the positives tapered off after that. The Fiery Chicken turned out to be little more than diced chicken and onions with minimal flavour — hardly a “fiery” dish worth the name. We also tried two types of pasta (white sauce and red sauce), but both were meager in quantity given the price point, leaving us unsatisfied. One thing that stood out in a negative way was how limited the food menu itself was — for a place of this positioning, the absence of something as basic as a pizza was hard to believe. Service was another sore point: slow, lackadaisical, and not particularly attentive, even when the restaurant wasn’t packed. The ambience is nice and laid-back, and that’s genuinely where Plan B scores — it’s an Instagram-friendly, cozy space to hang out. But with inconsistent drinks, so-so service, limited food choices, and portions that don’t match the pricing, this place truly lives up to its name: Plan B. And honestly? It’s one I’d only pick if Plan A is nowhere in sight. Overall: 3/5.

I first visited this restaurant back in 2016, and I remember having a pretty good experience. The decor was very cute. Since then, they have actually renovated the place, and the atmosphere is quite nice now.

Looking at the menu, it hasn't changed much from before, and the drinks are still incredibly cheap. We ordered a mango juice and a mango shake, but I was really disappointed. My mango juice was clearly loaded with sugar and very watered down. My friend's mango shake was also very thin. It felt like the quality matched the price: cheap, but not good.

Despite that, the restaurant was still very crowded. Apparently, their food is supposed to be better, but since I didn't try any, I can't really comment on that. I just felt that the drinks were lacking.

text.text:
Hole in the Wall is the breakfast spot for a lot of people in Koramangala, and that’s exactly why you’ll almost always find a queue outside. It’s become a post-workout ritual for so many locals, especially on weekends, so the place gets packed pretty quickly.

The food itself is good, but it’s not anything extraordinary. It’s simple, comforting breakfast food that’s done well. I ordered the English Breakfast, and it was decent—nothing mind-blowing, but definitely satisfying.

If you’re planning to visit, I’d recommend booking a table in advance if possible or getting there early to avoid the wait. And if the queue is too long, don’t stress—there are plenty of other nice cafés nearby that make for a good backup plan.

text.text:
If you are looking for a fantastic specialty coffee spot in Indiranagar that hits the mark on both brews and bakes, Beanlore is an absolute must-visit. The vibe here is perfect whether you’re catching up with a friend or settling in to get some laptop work done.

Hot Latte: The latte art (a perfectly executed heart) was beautiful, but the taste was even better. It is incredibly smooth, perfectly balanced, and has just the right amount of richness without being overly bitter.

Iced / Blended Coffee: Served in a super sleek, modern can-shaped glass with a striking green straw, this was a massive hit. It was perfectly frothy, creamy, and served as the ultimate refreshing pick-me-up.

The display counter is impossible to resist, especially if you visit during mango season.

Mango Pastries & Tarts: The fresh mango seasonal tarts and flaky puff pastries are loaded generously with perfectly ripe, juicy diced mangoes. They aren’t overly sweet, letting the natural flavor of the fruit shine.

Almond Croissants: Absolutely stellar. Golden, incredibly flaky, and generously topped with sliced almonds and a dusting of powdered sugar.

Classic Croissants & Brownies: The classic croissants have beautiful lamination and a rich, buttery flavor, while the walnut fudgy brownies on the side looked dense and decadent.

The aesthetic is clean and minimalist, down to their signature pale mint-green ceramic cups and saucers. The staff is efficient, and the seating is comfortable enough to easily spend a couple of hours here working or relaxing.

Highly recommended! Will definitely be coming back to try more of their roast profiles.

This new café on the block is an absolute gem. With its charming European vibe and thoughtfully designed interiors, it feels like stepping into a cozy corner of a vibrant street café. The space is warm, inviting, and effortlessly stylish — the kind of place you want to linger in.

The coffee is consistently excellent — rich, perfectly brewed, and clearly crafted with care. Their hot chocolate is hands down the best I’ve had: indulgent, velvety, and perfectly balanced. The matcha is equally impressive — smooth, vibrant, and beautifully prepared.

What truly makes this place special are the owners. They genuinely take the time to engage with guests, share recommendations, and make everyone feel welcome. It’s rare to find a café where exceptional drinks and heartfelt hospitality come together so seamlessly.

Definitely the cutest new spot in the neighborhood and a must-visit.

I genuinely don’t get the hype around Kink Coffee Shop, it’s subpar at best, and wildly overrated.

I tried their sea salt vanilla mocha expecting a decent specialty coffee. Instead, I got a cloying liquid dessert. Way too sweet, drowning in vanilla and salt, with almost zero actual coffee flavor.

It tasted like a milkshake that accidentally wandered into a coffee cup.

Specialty coffee is definitely not their specialty (they clearly missed the memo). Mediocre beans, sloppy execution, and gimmicky flavors that completely overpower the coffee.

Chill aesthetic if you’re there for the vibe, but if you actually want good coffee, skip this place. Your taste buds (and wallet) will thank you.

text.text:
The Grumpy Girl Cafe is one of those places that’s been heavily hyped on social media, which is what made us visit in the first place. Surprisingly though, the café was pretty empty even on a weekend.

The place itself is very chic and well maintained, with a cool old-school American diner vibe that gives it a fun and slightly different character compared to the usual Bangalore cafés.

One thing they definitely do well is variety especially when it comes to drinks. If you’re someone who enjoys trying different coffee-based beverages, you’ll probably like the menu here.

* The Iced Vietnamese Coffee was decent.
* The Strawberry Matcha Latte was actually pretty good and one of the better things we tried.

They also have a good range of bagels and snack options, making it a nice place to sit with friends and spend some time casually hanging out.

Pricing is definitely on the expensive side, with drinks costing around ₹400, but if you enjoy café culture and don’t mind paying for ambience and specialty drinks, the experience feels worth it.

They have limited options for veg and nonveg food, but based on whatever I had tried, they seem to do a decent job on that.

Nestled discreetly in a corner of a large, imposing building, this enchanting garden cafe is a hidden gem. Its theme, as the name suggests, is a beautifully maintained garden, a serene escape from the urban hustle. The cafe's thoughtful design and a limited number of tables create an intimate and cozy atmosphere, making it the perfect spot for quiet conversations. However, if you're with a large group, you might be a little disappointed as the space is better suited for smaller gatherings. The cafe offers a dedicated smoking area alongside non-smoking tables, catering to different preferences.

The menu is refreshingly concise, offering a curated selection of food and beverages. We enjoyed the Vietnamese cold coffee and a classic cold black coffee. The walnut tart was a delightful treat, but the surprise highlight was the hummus falafel salad, a fresh and flavorful choice. Overall, it's an excellent choice for a relaxed outing, ideal for catching up with friends or spending quality time with your loved one. The cafe’s charm lies in its peaceful ambiance and well-executed theme, making it a memorable spot to unwind.

text.text:
After seeing the promotions of this cafe, we travelled all the way from Kalyan Nagar to Indiranagar to try it out. We visited for lunch on Thursday and ordered avocado toast, a peri peri chicken sandwich, Golden Hour fresh juice (which was essentially orange juice), and Indigo Storm juice (a blend of purple cabbage, blueberries, and grapes).

Unfortunately, our experience was very disappointing. The avocado served in the toast was cold, straight out of the refrigerator, and appeared to be a couple of days old. After having the juices, we fell ill and were down with viral fever. We are not sure whether it was due to the quality of the fruits, water, or ice used, but we felt something was not right from the very first sip itself.

We are still recovering and have had to spend a significant amount on medical expenses. It is upsetting because we chose these items believing they were healthy options. In hindsight, I feel I would have been better off having a simple biryani and coke, which probably would not have resulted in such a large medical bill.

Beyond the financial impact, our health has been affected, and this experience has made us hesitant to trust claims of “healthy” food without concern for the quality and hygiene behind it.

The place is a hidden spot, located few lanes behind the other crowd favourites!
The cafe offers a small seating with a very limited but tasty menu!
We went for the crowd favourites that were the Cheese cakes and the brownies with ice cream.
The brownies were one of the best brownies I have tasted in my life! Soft and moist, which you generally don’t get anywhere. We loved it!
The cheesecake was equally good!
The best thing about the restaurant was the way they were preparing everything in batches. Every batch served warm and fresh!
However the place gets cramped up and since they are narrow and long, people were busy finding space.
The other problem was there were a lot of insects crawling around that leave a nasty sting!
They should work on it!
Rest the food was splendid!

The food/coffee/tea were genuinely good, and the overall experience started off well. However, the billing process at the end was disappointing. While calculating the total, the prices of items were increased by saying the menu prices had not been updated, resulting in around a 10% higher bill amount.

Paying a little extra isn’t really the issue when the quality is good, but changing prices at the time of billing without prior notice feels unfair to customers. It would be much better if the updated prices were clearly mentioned on the menu or displayed through a printed notice at the counter.

The place serves good tea and definitely has potential to grow further, but maintaining transparency and basic business standards is equally important. I hope this improves going forward because the quality is there — the customer experience just needs to match it.

text.text: Visited Circa based on a recommendation of a friend and was so pleased with my dining experience. It’s one of the quieter places located in prime Indiranagar and is meant to ensure you actually enjoy a lovely meal over a conversation instead of having to scream over loud music. The food is contemporary and you need to have a palette that is open to experimenting, to thoroughly enjoy the experience. We enjoyed pretty much every dish that was ordered, which is quite rare these days. The cocktails too are great and I would recommend you seek the advice of the owner/waiter. The place is a bit on the pricier side, but the overall great experience does justify the price to a large part. The place is not extensively promoted, and is positioned to do well purely based on word of mouth. Look forward to going back again. A special thank you to Ankit and his team for being great hosts.

Mr. A Singh is a highly knowledgeable individual in the area of speciality coffee. I always learn new things whenever I visit this roastery. Other than that, the quality of roasted coffees are second to none. They are one of the best when it comes to consistency (based on my purchases on monsooned malabar), and the taste. The details of roasted coffees also include a quality score which I've never seen in any other roasteries.

The price of coffee (both roasted coffees and coffees being served in care) is very reasonable in my opinion for such a high level of quality.

So if you are into speciality coffee or just love good coffee, or if you're a home barista, True Brew / GB roaster is a place to go in the heart of Indiranagar.

Attached images of my home brewed coffees. (Beans, Latte, Extraction of Monsooned Malabar)

text.text:
I have to start by saying this cafe is highly recommended. If you are a coffee lover, this is a must-visit spot in Bangalore.

Location & Vibe:
The cafe is situated right next to a sports club and football turf, which gives it a really unique and pleasant charm. It’s a great place to relax and watch some action while you enjoy your brew.

The Drinks:
• Espresso: I loved my coffee; it had those perfect fruity notes I was looking for.
• Hot Chocolate: This was impressive—very dense, thick, and rich.

The Food:
We ordered a pastrami sandwich and onion rings. Both were delicious and prepared well, making for a very satisfying meal alongside the drinks.

The Verdict:
I enjoyed the coffee so much that I even bought a bag of their coffee grounds to brew at home. Whether you're a serious coffee geek or just looking for a cool spot with a great vibe, Maverick & Farmer is excellent.

text.text:
I tried the Filter Ale and the Affogato here, and both are such wonderful combinations. I’m not usually a regular filter coffee drinker, so it was really nice to see these thoughtful twists on the coffee I generally see around. The slight sweetness and bubbles of the ginger ale balances out the bitterness of the coffee beautifully.

The affogato is just as good! They pour fresh filter coffee decoction over vanilla gelato, and you can really taste the quality of the ingredients. The gelato is incredibly creamy, not overly sweet, and it lets the coffee flavour shine instead of overpowering it. You get the best of both worlds!!

And it's also in a great spot! The surrounding environment is beautiful. There are all these huge, big old trees right outside the cafe, so it's really wonderful to just chill. It's not a very bustling road. The place is good, the coffee is good, the company is good (recommended to take your friends along ;P)

text.text:
Beanlore Coffee Roasters – A Perfect Little Date Night Spot

Visited Beanlore Coffee Roasters with my wife for a cozy date night, and it turned out to be a really lovely experience. The place has a calm and relaxing vibe, making it perfect for spending quality time over good food and coffee.

What We Tried:
* Fried Rice with Chicken Stir Fry Bowl
Flavorful, satisfying, and well-balanced. The chicken was nicely cooked and paired really well with the rice.
* Korean Bun
Soft, delicious, and packed with flavor. A unique item that was worth trying.
* Strawberry Mascarpone Croissant
Light, buttery, and beautifully balanced with the sweetness of strawberry and creamy mascarpone. Easily one of the highlights.
* Jade Cream
Refreshing and smooth with a unique flavor profile.
* Hot Chocolate
Rich, comforting, and perfect for the cozy café atmosphere.

Overall Experience:
- Cozy and relaxing ambiance for couples
- Tasty food and well-made beverages
- Great café vibe for conversations and date nights
- Desserts and drinks were especially enjoyable

Rating: 4.5/5

Overall, it was a really good date night with tasty food, comforting drinks, and a pleasant atmosphere. A lovely place to unwind and spend quality time with someone special.

text.text:
Magnolia Bakery

One of the most popular dessert spots in Bangalore, Magnolia Bakery is definitely worth visiting if you enjoy desserts. The bakery has a beautiful white, minimal, Victorian-inspired aesthetic that gives it a classic New York bakery feel.

Must-tries:
• Vanilla Tres Leches – Easily my favourite. Light, moist and perfectly balanced without being overly sweet.
• Hummingbird Cupcake – I’m usually not a cupcake person, but this one genuinely surprised me. Definitely one of the best things on the menu.
• Red Velvet Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting – The cream cheese frosting is what makes this dessert. It complements the cake really well and makes it worth ordering.
• Hot Chocolate – Rich, comforting and a great choice if you’re visiting during the evenings worth the price.

Good, but not perfect:
• Classic Banana Pudding – One of their signature desserts and definitely worth trying, but it can feel slightly too sweet for many people.
• Pecan Cheesecake – Decent, but it didn’t particularly stand out to me compared to the other desserts.
• Coffee – Good enough to pair with dessert, but I wouldn’t visit just for the coffee.

Could be better:
• Chocolate Cake with Vanilla Buttercream – It honestly reminded me of a good Iyengar Bakery chocolate cake. It wasn’t bad, but for almost ₹500 a slice, I expected a more memorable experience.

Overall, Magnolia Bakery shines with its signature desserts rather than every item on the menu. If you’re visiting for the first time, I’d recommend sticking to the Vanilla Tres Leches, Hummingbird Cupcake and the Red Velvet Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting. Those alone make the visit worthwhile.

We went there to get desserts after a sumptuous lunch at a nearby restaurant. The place had just opened a week back. The shop itself is small with a simple counter where you can place your order. They do not keep any display of their products to visually help you browse and decide. In that, I would think having a set of display elements would help customers in deciding.

On the food itself, I went there will high hopes given the reel I had seen and the reviews that I had read. But I must say I was disappointed. We ordered a Blueberry Signature Kisses, a Nutella No Bake Cheesecake and a Ferrero Rocher Milk Cake. Of them, the Milk Cake was better one. The Blueberry compote was overpowering. The bases in the desserts are the same in their category. And with different toppings. So be aware of that.

Their packaging is nice. And the person at counter is pleasant and helpful.

If you are one who is particular about their desserts, this place is not for you.

text.text:
Lick – Lavonne Ice Cream Kitchen is a must-visit if you love premium, creative ice creams. The place is quite large and often crowded, which says a lot about how popular it is.

We tried a wide range of items including the Mango Tres Leches sundae, Smoked Dark Chocolate, Cookies n Cream, The Ultimate Pistachio, roasted almond brownie, and the Squats and Scoops sundae. Everything was top-notch, rich, creamy, and full of flavour. The Smoked Dark Chocolate and Ultimate Pistachio (very rich, you might not be able to finish it) really stood out, and the sundaes were indulgent and well put together.

One of the best parts was being able to taste almost all the flavours before deciding. The staff were very informative and patient, explaining the different options and helping us choose what suited our taste.

Their cookies, or “bookies” as they call them, are also exceptional and pair really well with the ice creams. Do try their Hallelujah, lemon raspberry, German Chocolate.

Yes, the pricing is on the higher side, but the quality, creativity, and overall experience make it worth it. Definitely a great spot for dessert lovers in Indiranagar.

Their cookies, or “bookies” as they call them, are also exceptional and pair really well with the ice creams. Do try their Hallelujah, lemon raspberry, German Chocolate.

text.text:
If you are looking for high-quality, artisanal ice cream in Indiranagar, this place is serving up some total bangers. The quality of the ingredients is evident in every scoop, and they are doing some really interesting things with their flavor profiles.

**The Standout Scoops**
* **Protein Chocolate:** A huge win. It’s rare to find a high-protein version that actually tastes this good—perfect for a post-workout treat or a slightly healthier indulgence.

* **Ultimate Pistachio:** Rich, nutty, and incredibly authentic.

* **Watermelon Feta:** A refreshing, experimental flavor that works surprisingly well for the summer.

**The Reality Check**

* **The Pricing:** It is slightly on the pricier side considering the serving sizes. While the quality is premium, it feels like a splurge.

* **The Seating:** This is the main drawback. There are only about **4 stools inside with AC**. In the middle of a Bangalore summer, sitting outside in the scorching sun isn't ideal—your ice cream ends up melting faster than you can enjoy it!

* **Availability:** I’m really rooting for them to bring in even more healthy/functional versions of their classics.

**Final Verdict**
The ice cream itself is 9/10. If they can work on the pricing, expand the indoor seating, and lean further into those "healthier" versions, this place would be perfect. Definitely worth a visit for the flavors alone, but maybe aim for a late-evening trip when it's cooler!

In fact, I discovered this bakery by accident while visiting the Wrogn store. Since the bakery is connected to the store with no wall in between, I couldn’t resist stepping inside. The sweet, delicious aroma was absolutely mouth-watering and kept drawing me in.

As I looked around their shelves, I noticed a wide variety of items—ranging from dry snacks to pastries to ice cream. Their collection is really big, and everything seemed to be made with high-quality ingredients. Of course, since the quality is high, the prices are also on the higher side.

To be honest, coming from a small town probably makes me feel this bakery is a bit expensive. But when I think of Bengaluru and the lifestyle here, the prices actually seem quite normal. The place also has a very comfortable ambiance, perfect for enjoying snacks with your kids and loved ones.

I tried some snacks and cream rolls, and cookies which were really tasty, though a bit pricey. But that’s fine, since I don’t visit often.

I’d definitely recommend this place, especially if you have kids or if you’re someone whose taste buds are always looking for delicious bakery treats.

Gelato Ice Cream -
NOTE:
Taste testing is not allowed due to hygeine protocols

1. Strawberry - 2.5/5 (People who like Tangy Flavors will love this, I did not enjoy this personally)
2. French Vanilla - 4.5 ( Super Smooth, very light and mind blowing Taste)
3. Wildberry - 2.5/5 ( Again people who like Tangy Flavors will Enjoy this, did not enjoy this personally)
4. Truffle - 4/5 ( people who like Chocolate should definitely go for this, not too chocolately, not too sweet , just the right taste)
5. Choco Wafer - 4/5 ( The wafers added in this really bring in the taste, absolute bomb)

About the Place -
1. Small and Compact
2. Chill Ambience, good place to come with Friends

Cost -
1.So instead of Charging 60/70/80/90 rs for a Single Flavor, you pay for the Cup Size - Regular(120)/Medium(180)/Large
2. I had 1 Regular and 1 Medium
3. You can add any 2 Flavors in Regular and 3 Flavors in Medium
4. Place was clean Inside and Outside
5. No Handwash, Just tissues
6. Vegetarians who do not eat Egg will not be able to Enjoy their pies, macaroons, different breads,etc
7. Popsicles were also available

I ordered 6 bambolonis and got them delivered to my office near the TGND location. Delivery through Porter was quick — around 20 minutes — but that’s about the only good thing I can say.
The items arrived completely melted and had pooled inside the packaging. It was a mess, and honestly not what I expected at all. The quality and presentation were way off from what was shown.

Having ordered the same from my hometown before, I can tell the difference — it was freshly made, well-packed, and tasted so much better. This experience was nowhere close to that standard.
Hoping the team works on better packaging and quality control, especially for deliveries. 🙁

text.text:
Celadine Bakehouse is the latest gem I’ve discovered for indulging in authentic New York–style cookies. I first came across their creations during my visit to Koreyaki, Indiranagar, where they sell Celadine’s cookies and their signature Korean Cream Buns. After that first bite, I was completely hooked and have been a loyal fan ever since.

Most of their cookies are priced between ₹150 and ₹200 per piece, and the quality truly justifies the price. They use premium and imported ingredients like Lotus Biscoff biscuits, Ferrero Rocher, macadamia nuts from Australia, and rich Belgian chocolate to create cookies that are both luscious and tempting. During one of my recent visits to their baking unit in Indiranagar, I had the pleasure of meeting Priya, the owner and the creative mind behind Celadine Bakehouse. Her passion for baking and dedication to perfecting her craft clearly reflect in every product they offer.

They offer both egg and eggless variants, with an impressive spread of flavors such as:

Nutella

Marshmallow (₹150)

Barbados (₹150)

Choco Chunk (₹150)

Lotus Biscoff (₹200)

Double Choco Chunk (₹200)

Triple Choco Chunk

Cowboy (₹200)

Snickerdoodle (₹100) (A Buttery cookie coated in cinnamon Sugar)

Nutella Fudge Brownie (₹150)

Biscoff Blondie (₹200)

New York Cheesecake (₹200)

Tiramisu Tub (₹250)

Korean Cream Bun (₹250)

Half Moon (₹200)

You can get them from Koreyaki outlets in Indiranagar or Kalyan Nagar, though the selection there is limited. For the full range, it’s best to buy directly from their baking unit or through Swiggy (with a slight price difference). They also deliver to all areas across Bangalore with a small delivery charge, and the packaging is simply amazing and aesthetically pleasing.  They also accept bulk orders, which can be placed via their Instagram page or WhatsApp.

Priya herself is a delight to interact with warm, friendly, and ever ready to help you choose the perfect cookie based on your taste preferences. You can see her genuine love for what she does, and that warmth translates beautifully into the taste of every cookie.

My Personal Favorites

It’s hard to pick just one, but my top picks would be:

Barbados – Made with 55% Belgian chocolate, a total melt-in-the-mouth indulgence

Choco Chunk – Classic and comforting

Lotus Biscoff – That caramelized crunch is addictive

Triple Chocolate – Chocolate heaven for chocoholics

Snickerdoodle and Marshmallow – Soft, sweet, and perfectly balanced

Korean Bun

Tiramisu -  Tiramisu was really luscious

Celadine Bakehouse is a must-try for every cookie lover in Bengaluru. Their cookies are not only perfect for personal indulgence but also make excellent gifts or dessert options for home gatherings, corporate events, or festive occasions.

text.text:
If you're looking for an indulgent vegan bakery to satisfy your colossal sweet tooth in a jiffy, Pibbles is possibly the perfect spot for you. They mean it when they say they're your local sugar dealer!

Their chocolate-based sweet treats are, in my opinion, their best offerings. Among them, the Rum Choco Cherry pastry is my all-time fave.

If I had to nitpick, the only downside would be the minimal (only seats six) seating arrangement.

By and large, heartily recommended — even to non-vegans or the vegan-curious.

PS: A sincere note of appreciation for the owner, Gouri Koushik, for her stellar customer engagement and warm hospitality — thank you! :)

Indiranagar, Nirula's Restaurant is a hidden gem waiting to be discovered. Despite its unassuming facade, this place offers a delightful dining experience perfect for a quick bite or a leisurely meal.
The ambiance at Nirula's is inviting, with a cozy interior and two balcony seating options, adding a touch of charm to your dining experience. Whether you're catching up with friends or enjoying a solo meal, the ambiance sets the perfect backdrop.
One of the highlights of Nirula's is undoubtedly its diverse menu, offering both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options that are sure to tantalize your taste buds. Having sampled both, I can attest to the deliciousness of their offerings. The pizza and burgers are standout items, bursting with flavor and cooked to perfection. The paneer dim sum is a must-try, showcasing the restaurant's culinary expertise.
The pizzas at Nirula's are a true delight, with options for both thin crust and regular crust lovers. Whether you prefer a lighter bite or a more indulgent experience, both varieties deliver on taste and quality. Even the regular crust pizza maintains a perfect balance, with a not-too-thick crust that enhances the overall enjoyment of the dish.
From the inviting ambiance to the delectable food and wallet-friendly prices, Nirula's Restaurant exudes a vibe that keeps diners coming back for more. Whether you're a local resident or just passing through, this underrated gem is worth a visit.

I’ve had this cafe on my bucket list for ages, and after finally visiting this weekend, I can confirm: it’s worth every bit of the hype.
The food experience was standout.
The Turkish Omelette was the undisputed star of the show—easily my absolute favorite—though the Lavonne Breakfast Platter was a very solid contender.
As a recent matcha convert, their Vanilla Matcha hit all the right notes, and the staff-recommended Blueberry Smoothie was genuinely top-notch.

I even grabbed a loaf of their Sourdough to go, and it’s just as high-quality as the dine-in menu.
A few things to note:
• The Wait: Getting a reservation is a mission, so plan well in advance.
• The Price: It’s definitely on the pricier side, so keep that in mind for your budget.
Overall, it’s a must-visit for any foodie!

Overall: Go for the pizza 🍕, skip the pasta (at least this one).

text.text:
I have visited Naturals Ice Cream on two different occasions, both during weekends, and overall it has been a good experience.

Location:
The outlet is located in one of the busiest streets of Indiranagar, making it very easy to find.

Space & Crowd:
The shop is quite compact, with limited indoor seating (around 10–15 people max). On weekends, it gets crowded, and both times we visited, there was a queue of about 5 minutes. Seating is limited, so most people end up standing outside and enjoying their ice cream.

Menu Variety:
They offer a wide range of options including classic ice creams, seasonal fruit-based flavours, sorbets, and cone/cup servings. The seasonal fruit flavours are a highlight.

What We Tried & Ratings:

First Visit:
Tender Coconut – 4.5/5: Very refreshing and light, with small coconut bits that add to the texture. Definitely one of the better flavours.

Malai Khurma – 3.5/5: Creamy and decent. It tastes somewhat similar to rasmalai, which may appeal to those who like traditional dessert flavours.

Second Visit:
Mango Ice Cream – 2/5: Slightly disappointing. It felt a bit stale and didn’t have the freshness you’d expect from a fruit-based flavour.

Malai Pista – 4.5/5: Very good. Creamy with a mild nutty flavour—well balanced and enjoyable.

Overall Experience:
The quality of ice cream is generally good, especially for their signature and creamy flavours. However, consistency can vary (as seen with the mango flavour). The crowd and limited seating are the only downsides.

Final Verdict:
A good place to try natural and seasonal ice creams in Indiranagar. Worth a visit, but be prepared for crowds on weekends and choose flavours wisely.
