text.text:
Stepping into this hidden gem feels less like entering a local business and more like discovering a curated sanctuary for the senses. While the cafe is intimate in scale, comfortably accommodating small parties of two to four, its physical footprint is far outweighed by its immense character. The aesthetic is a triumph of minimalist sophistication; the interior is meticulously designed with a stark black-and-white palette that exudes a timeless, classic elegance. For anyone who appreciates a clean, high-contrast visual environment, the atmosphere alone is worth the visit.

The Culinary Highlights:

The menu, though focused, delivers high-impact & variety of desserts and beverages. We opted for the signature pairings:
• The Signature Coconut Coffee: This is not merely a beverage; it is a revelation. The infusion of tropical coconut notes with a robust coffee base creates a singular flavour profile that is both daring and perfectly balanced. It is a rare find that manages to be "unique" without sacrificing drinkability—truly an exceptional brew.
• The Chocolate Tart: A masterpiece of texture and taste. The tart shell possesses a superior crispness that provides a satisfying snap, acting as the perfect vessel for its rich, decadent chocolate filling.

From the coordinated decor to the artisanal quality of the refreshments, every detail feels intentional. Whether you are a coffee aficionado or a lover of sleek interior design, this spot is an absolute must-visit. I cannot recommend it highly enough for those seeking a quiet, stylish corner to enjoy a truly innovative caffeine fix.

text.text:
​I tried the 7-course tasting menu at Minibé, and honestly, the team is killing it. It was 3 savory dishes and 4 desserts, followed by petit fours and hibiscus tea. Every single bit of it was spot on.
​They’re doing a great job of taking seasonal stuff and making it feel high-end without losing the soul. Some of the highlights:
​The Savory Cannoli: Using fried avarebele and an avarebele mousse was genius. Such a cool way to use that ingredient.
​Chicken Ballotine: This came with a pumpkin and carrot velouté and panisse. The reduced jus was rich and tied everything together perfectly.
​The Desserts: That yogurt cheese ice cream is dangerous—I could’ve eaten a massive bowl of just that. The berries and barley course worked so well together, and their version of Gajar ka Halwa actually caught me off guard in a good way.
​The Finisher: Even the chocolate dessert showed off some serious technique. But my absolute favorite was the choux pastry with chocolate crème pât from the petit fours.
​Great vibes, food. If you appreciate good technique and local ingredients, you need to check them out.
Between the food and the conversations, it was a fab evening!
​

text.text:
A nice small place near the 80ft road in Indiranagar.
We tried two things. The molleaux au chocolat and the black sesame cheesecake.
The presentation was very nice. Serving size if decent, almost value for money.
This place definitely qualifies for gourmet desserts. The molleaux had a symphony of different flavours. It was a nice balance of overpowering and subtle flavours. The caramel drops did act as the bridge between the strong chocolate flavour in the molleaux and the subtly crispiness of the side waffery thing (I am forgetting what the chef called it). All in all, a refreshing dessert.
Then comes the black sesame cheesecake. I was completely mesmerised with their take on the cheesecake. As an engineer with a mechanical background, it almost felt like an exploded view of a cheesecake.
It felt like the time has stop and the cheesecake was its exploded view and I get to choose what to pair with what. The black sesame bread did pair well with their in-house vanilla ice cream. The crumbs beneath it felt like the analogous of the usual biscotti in the cheesecake. The strawberry marmalade like thingie on the side was pairing everything well together. I dont think so the dish would have gone together if a single piece was missing.
Yet, both the dishes had just the optimal number of pieces without it becoming too much for the mind to process.
All in all, a nice place. If you have the budget for gourmet desserts then do visit this place.

The caramel drops did act as the bridge between the strong chocolate flavour in the molleaux and the subtly crispiness of the side waffery thing (I am forgetting what the chef called it). All in all, a refreshing dessert.
Then comes the black sesame cheesecake. I was completely mesmerised with their take on the cheesecake. As an engineer with a mechanical background, it almost felt like an exploded view of a cheesecake.
It felt like the time has stop and the cheesecake was its exploded view and I get to choose what to pair with what. The black sesame bread did pair well with their in-house vanilla ice cream. The crumbs beneath it felt like the analogous of the usual biscotti in the cheesecake. The strawberry marmalade like thingie on the side was pairing everything well together. I dont think so the dish would have gone together if a single piece was missing.
Yet, both the dishes had just the optimal number of pieces without it becoming too much for the mind to process.
All in all, a nice place. If you have the budget for gourmet desserts then do visit this place.

text.text:
The initial approach to this venue is, frankly, unsettling. The entrance is decidedly eerie, bordering on scary, which doesn’t exactly scream "fine dining." However, crossing the threshold reveals a surprising transformation.
The interior is beautifully designed, offering a stark, aesthetic contrast to the exterior. More importantly, the climate control is a literal lifesaver; the temperature inside is perfectly calibrated to provide a refreshing escape from the sweltering heat outside.

We arrived for Sunday brunch at 1:00 PM and were the only patrons there. Even by the time we departed at 4:00 PM, the space remained curiously empty.
While this makes it an ideal spot to chill with friends for hours without being rushed, the culinary experience fails to live up to the decor.
The menu is disappointingly limited.
The Kodagu Pork Taco and Pandi Pork were highlights (4/5), boasting authentic flavors. We even went off-menu for a Prawn Butter Garlic (3/5) since all listed prawn dishes were fried.
However, the Asian Chicken Wings were an absolute disaster (0/5).
On the beverage side, the Garden Fresh gin cocktail and the Daiquiri were well-executed (4/5), though the Curried Pineapple felt like an odd experiment that didn't quite land.

Ultimately, while the ambiance is serene, the inconsistent food means I cannot recommend a visit.

That said, hoping the next visit will be better,the place has the potential to deliver a truly solid experience if service consistency is maintained from beginning to end.

This completely ruined our dining experience and raised serious questions about the restaurant’s food preparation and cleanliness practices.

Food safety should be a basic expectation at any restaurant, and finding an insect in a served dish is unacceptable. Although the ambiance may be good, hygiene cannot be compromised. I hope the management takes immediate corrective action, conducts a thorough inspection of their kitchen, and improves their quality control processes to ensure this does not happen to other customers.

Unfortunately, based on this experience, I cannot recommend this place.

Visited this place in Indiranagar recently and honestly, the experience was a mixed bag. We had a reservation for 8 PM for a group of five, but still had to wait almost an hour for our table, which was quite frustrating. Since we had invited others as well, we decided to stay instead of looking for another place.

While waiting, we checked out the bar area and tried the Reviver mocktail, which was pretty average and not something I’d personally recommend.

Once we got seated, we started with the Dahi Kebabs (3/5), California Sushi Roll (4/5), peri-peri fries (really good), and paneer tikka, which was just okay. Later, I tried their Strawberry Cheesecake cocktail and that was honestly the highlight for me. If you enjoy Bacardi/white rum-based drinks, this one is definitely worth trying again.

For the main course, we ordered dal makhani, paneer butter masala, naan, and rotis. The food was noticeably spicy, so if you’re sensitive to spice levels, it’s better to ask them to tone it down beforehand.

Overall, despite a few good dishes and drinks, the long waiting time made the experience underwhelming for me. Personally, I don’t see myself visiting again.

The only standout dish was the Honey Chilli Lotus Stem, which was genuinely delicious. The Fish Koliwada was decent but nothing memorable. Blueberry panacotta wasn't what I was expecting.
Would I visit again? Unfortunately, no.

Overall, it was a decent experience, mainly because of the food, but a few aspects could definitely be improved.

text.text:
Recently visited Porcupine, the newly opened Indian public house on Indiranagar 100ft Road. The ambiance is one of the biggest highlights with warm lighting, exposed brick walls, vintage record displays, classy bar seating, and a cozy premium vibe throughout the place. They also have upstairs seating and an outdoor section, though outdoor seating at night can get slightly uncomfortable because of mosquitoes.

The menu has a good collection of both veg and non veg dishes including starters, pizzas, burgers, kulchas, and mains. The non veg section mainly consists of chicken, fish, lamb/mutton, prawns, pork, and egg based dishes. They also have a dedicated dessert section named Sweet Spot along with hot beverages such as filter coffee, black coffee, hot chocolate, green tea, and more. The bar menu includes blended whiskeys, single malt whiskeys, imported wines, Indian style cocktails, and other alcohol options. Prices are definitely on the higher side because of the location factor.

Tried the Tropical Trouble mocktail priced at Rs 199. It is basically a chilled pineapple based drink with a sweet tangy punch. It tasted refreshing but felt too sweet and had a lot of ice cubes which made the quantity feel less for the price.

For food, ordered the Roast Chicken Pizza priced at Rs 560. It comes with a hand stretched crust topped with roast chicken, mozzarella, and herbs. The taste was decent overall, but the amount of chicken pieces on the pizza felt quite less, making it feel slightly overpriced.

Also tried the Dirty Stack dessert priced at Rs 420 from the dessert section. It is a layered chocolate cake served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. The dessert tasted extra sweet once both were mixed together and felt like a normal dessert without anything extraordinary. Personally did not feel it was worth the pricing.

Service was good and the staffs were polite and attentive throughout. One thing to note is that service charge is added to the bill, but it is optional.

Overall, Porcupine is a nice place with a really good ambiance and relaxed Indian public house vibe. A good spot for dates, casual meetups, drinks, and laid back conversations with friends. Valet parking is available and it is better to reserve tables through EazyDiner or Dineout for discounts and easier seating during weekends.

Worth a visit for sure..

text.text:
SOKA is the kind of bar that feels like a well-kept secret the moment you step inside — and then immediately becomes a place you can’t stop thinking about. Located in the heart of Indiranagar, this 38-seat gem has already earned widespread acclaim (ranked No. 28 in Asia’s 50 Best Bars 2025), and for good reason.

From the street you might miss it, but once inside, SOKA reveals itself like a work of art. The moment you enter, your eye is drawn up to the dramatic centerpiece: a 4-foot cocoon lamp that casts a warm, golden glow across the room. Copper scales flow down a 15-foot wall, their patina catching the light, and the bar’s front is crafted of beaten copper patterned with waves and scales — a tactile, maritime motif that threads through the entire space.

SOKA is also an Omakase bar in the truest sense. You don’t simply order cocktails off a menu; you give yourself over to a carefully curated, bartender-led journey. Avinash Kapoli and his team configure bespoke liquid narratives, riffing on classic techniques while introducing unexpected local touches. The bar’s ten-metre kitchen is astonishingly compact — touted as one of the smallest bar kitchens in the country — yet it’s engineered for precision and speed. The result is a seamless choreography between bartender and chef: drinks are paired with micro-plates, and each course dovetails with the next so the evening feels like a single, evolving performance rather than a series of discrete orders.

The food at SOKA is served in nano plates — tiny masterpieces that pack visionary flavour into small formats. Each plate reframes a familiar ingredient through inventive technique: think chhena at the center of a kulcha, jackfruit partnering with artichoke, or aged cheese folded into fruit-forward canapés. The micro-plates are designed to be shared, nibbled, and discussed, and they pair beautifully with the layered cocktails. The kitchen’s compactness belies its ambition: texture, temperature, and contrast are all meticulously considered.

A few highlights that lingered with us:
- Spicy Smoked Kulcha — a playful nano plate where a chhena core meets artichoke and jackfruit. The smoke and spice lift the creamy center, while the bread element keeps it grounded and comforting.
- Pi Pi Martini — made with Hapusa gin, jujube-pickled brine and dry vermouth. It’s saline, aromatic and deeply satisfying — a delicate balance of savory and botanical notes.
- Mofo Don — premium tequila with pickled pineapple, red cabbage, cilantro and jalapeño. This one is bold, bright and tropical with an edge of heat that hangs around in the best way.
- Mysore High — Bacardi Anejo Cuatro combined with Mysore banana oleo saccharum, coffee liqueur and aromatic bitters. A thoughtful nod to regional ingredients that finishes rich and complex.
- I Blame Jasmine — Hapusa gin with a carbonated jasmine cordial. Floral, lifted and utterly drinkable.
- Cheese Cherry Pineapple — Bacardi carta blanca with pineapple, aged cheddar, cream cheese and luxardo cherry; the contrast of savory cheese and bright fruit is unexpectedly brilliant.
- Soka Represent — Grey Goose vodka, Campari, grapefruit, saline and a feather-light vegan foam. Bitter, citrusy, and perfectly balanced.

SOKA’s intimate size is one of its charms; the room hums but doesn’t roar. Conversation is possible, the staff can focus on each guest, and the energy remains high without becoming overwhelming. The long communal table, banquette seating and the bar itself all offer slightly different moods — cozy, social, contemplative — yet each spot feels connected to the central performance.

What makes SOKA extraordinary is how it balances two impulses that don’t often sit together: refinement and mischief. Cocktails are elevated and elegant, yet full of humour and surprise; nano plates are small but full of technical finesse and heart. It’s rare to find a place that can be so precise — in presentation, in temperature, in pairing — and still so welcoming.

Recently visited Soka and unfortunately, it didn’t live up to expectations.
The space felt loud and cramped, which made it difficult to relax or even hold a proper conversation. Cocktails were below par for the price, lacking both flavour and refinement, and most of them came with a massive block of ice that left the drink watery almost instantly. The food tasted okay (mind you nothing extraordinary at all), but portion sizes were disappointingly small.

Some elite guests may pretend to enjoy the place for the vibe, but if you care about value and quality, the experience falls short.
Given everything, the pricing felt completely unjustified. There are many other bars offering better ambience, better drinks and real value for money.

Wouldn’t recommend unless they rethink their pricing/quality/quantity and significantly improve what they are trying to offer/achieve !!

This makes for the perfect place to have a joyful evening with your friends.

text.text:
If you’re looking for a typical loud bar in Bangalore… this is not it.
403 Forbidden is easily one of the most unique cocktail experiences in the city. The whole concept revolves around “distractions denied,” and you can actually feel that the moment you step in. It’s more like a theatre disguised as a bar, where everything—from lighting to music to the way drinks are served—is designed to make you slow down and be present.
The cocktails here are the real highlight. We tried their skinny cocktails—“Let’s Start Skinny” and “Life in a Metro”—both were super well-balanced, refreshing, and didn’t feel heavy at all.
Food-wise, we tried quite a mix—loved the edamame and chestnut dimsum, the mini coin paratha with paneer, and the soba noodle bowl. Also tried a couple of non-veg starters recommended by the team, and they were equally good.
The vibe is intimate, slightly mysterious, and a refreshing change from the usual high-energy nightlife spots. Perfect for meaningful conversations or just enjoying a well-made drink without the chaos.
Service was warm and knowledgeable, with great recommendations that actually added to the experience.
Overall, not just a bar—it’s an experience. Definitely one of those places you go to when you want something different and memorable.
📍 Indiranagar, Bangalore

However, the food didn’t quite match the setting. We ordered a variety of starters, but most of them felt repetitive — same base, overly saucy, and a bit too spicy. The flavours seemed to clash and overpower each other rather than complementing the dishes.

Overall, it’s a decent spot if you're looking for a nice place to hang out, but the food could definitely use more variety and balance. I'd rate it average, mainly for the ambience and service.

Visited Bohemian with a group of friends on a Saturday night, and unfortunately, the experience was disappointing from the very beginning.

Before even taking our order, the waiter informed us that the service charge was mandatory. Starting the dining experience with that conversation left a poor first impression.

The food itself was average at best and felt significantly overpriced. Given the menu prices, we expected generous portions, but each serving was barely enough for one person.

Another major issue was the number of mosquitoes around the seating area, which made it difficult to enjoy the meal.

The restaurant also uses a web-based menu instead of a physical one, which wasn’t very user-friendly. To make matters worse, an additional ₹30 platform fee was added to the bill, which felt unnecessary and wasn’t something we expected.

Overall, the combination of average food, small portions, mosquitoes, and extra charges made the experience poor. I wouldn’t consider returning.

Second visit and likely the last. Found parking, waited 5 to 10 minutes, and not a single staff member acknowledged us. Pathetic service and complete apathy from the servers. Overall, a clean and pleasant place with good fundamentals. With more flexibility and empowerment at the service level, the experience could be stronger.

text.text:
A Seamless Blend of Craftsmanship, Flavour, and Atmosphere.

Daffy’s delivers a vibrant and well-curated dining experience within the Arena space in Indiranagar, offering a seamless blend of lively ambiance, quality food, and thoughtfully crafted beverages. The setting strikes a fine balance between energetic and comfortable, making it an ideal choice for both casual outings and relaxed social gatherings.
A standout from the visit was the Hefeweizen smooth, refreshing, and beautifully brewed with a balanced flavor profile that reflects attention to detail and consistency. It pairs exceptionally well with the Kung Pao Chicken, which was equally impressive. The dish was perfectly executed, offering a delightful combination of spice, texture, and depth of flavor without overpowering the palate.
The service was attentive, with staff maintaining a warm and welcoming approach throughout. The overall atmosphere adds to the experience, with ample seating and a layout that accommodates both small and larger groups comfortably.
Daffy’s stands out as a dependable destination for those seeking quality food and well-crafted brews in a lively yet relaxed environment. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy a well-rounded dining experience in one of Bangalore’s most popular social hubs.

Consistently Memorable Experience
Returning to Daffy’s for a second visit reaffirmed its place as a dependable and thoughtfully curated dining destination within the Arena space in Indiranagar. The ambiance continues to strike a perfect balance between lively and relaxed, creating an inviting setting for a comfortable and enjoyable outing.
What truly elevated this visit was the personalised and attentive service. Pao Min stood out for his exceptional hospitality he thoughtfully remembered my previous visit and was considerate about my earlier dental treatment, initially suggesting softer food options. Once I shared that I had recovered, he warmly assisted in selecting a dish, recommending the mutton crispy fry, which turned out to be an excellent choice flavourful, well-textured, and perfectly executed.
The peanut salad was equally delightful, offering a fresh and vibrant combination of flavours that paired beautifully with the pineapple and lemongrass beer—refreshing and well-balanced, enhancing the overall dining experience.
I left feeling completely uplifted by the experience. The combination of attentive service, well-crafted dishes, and a welcoming atmosphere makes Daffy’s a place worth returning to.

Exceptional food, cozy vibes, and solid drinks 🍽️✨

Visited The Native, Indiranagar, and honestly, it turned out to be one of those places where everything just hits right. The taste is absolutely top notch and every single dish we tried was packed with flavour and authenticity.

I completely fell in love with the Anjal Tawa Fry. It was perfectly cooked, beautifully spiced, and easily the highlight of the meal. Apart from that, the chicken ghee roast, pepper chicken, and other tawa fry dishes were outstanding. Paired with soft neer dosa, the combination was chef’s kiss 🤌 Whatever we ordered was consistently good, which says a lot about the kitchen.

They also have a good selection of booze, which complements the food really well and makes it a great place for a relaxed lunch or dinner with friends.

The ambience deserves a mention too. Cozy, warm, and comfortable, without being too loud or cramped. It’s the kind of place where you can sit back, enjoy good food, good drinks, and have proper conversations.

Overall, The Native delivers on taste, quality, and vibe. If you enjoy coastal flavours, well cooked non veg, and a cozy dining experience, this place is a must visit. Definitely coming back to try more from the menu.

I didn’t try any drinks, but the pricing looked quite affordable. Food prices are reasonable as well.
Overall, it’s a good place to hang out and have a decent time, especially with friends.

text.text:
Visited Chin Lung Brewery Indiranagar recently and the place definitely stands out for its energetic nightlife vibe and buzzing crowd. The ambience is lively, especially during weekends, with good music, multiple seating areas, and a proper Bangalore brewery atmosphere. Their craft beers are decent, especially for casual hangouts with friends, and the food menu has some good bar-style options like tandoori items, nachos, and starters. The staff was polite overall, though service can get slightly slow when the place becomes fully packed.

What I liked most was the vibe — it feels like one of those places where people come to chill for hours, watch matches, enjoy loud music, and have a fun evening. The interiors and lighting add to the experience, making it a good option for group outings and weekend plans.

However, the place gets extremely crowded during peak hours, and waiting time for tables can become frustrating. Parking is also limited, so valet becomes the only practical option. Some dishes were excellent while a few felt average, so the food experience can be slightly inconsistent depending on what you order.

Overall, Chin Lung Brewery is worth visiting if you’re looking for a lively brewery experience in Indiranagar with good ambience, crowd, and casual party vibes. Best enjoyed with friends during evenings, especially if you like loud music and a happening atmosphere.

text.text:
Vesparo impressed me with its stunning dimly lit ambience and thoughtfully curated new cocktail menu.

Inspired by a journey across Asia, each cocktail captures the flavors and drinking culture of a different destination while paying tribute to Asia’s 50 Best Bars. If you love creative cocktails with a story behind them, this place is definitely worth visiting.

I tried the Oh My Jasmine, inspired by Singapore, and it was easily my favorite. The floral notes of jasmine paired beautifully with matcha and whisky, creating a smooth yet bold cocktail.

I also loved the Sabai Sabai, inspired by Thailand. The refreshing blend of spiced rum, sugarcane, makrut lime, lavender, and lemongrass made it light, citrusy, and incredibly easy to sip.

I came in for one drink but ended up staying for more. Paired with the succulent Paneer Ghee Roast and flavorful Drunken Chicken, it was the perfect way to end a weekday evening.

I also loved the Sabai Sabai, inspired by Thailand. The refreshing blend of spiced rum, sugarcane, makrut lime, lavender, and lemongrass made it light, citrusy, and incredibly easy to sip.

I came in for one drink but ended up staying for more. Paired with the succulent Paneer Ghee Roast and flavorful Drunken Chicken, it was the perfect way to end a weekday evening.

Would definitely come back, preferably for a weekend night out.

Do I drink(alcohol ofcourse)...?
No...
Do I stop visiting bars and breweries...?
Not yet all... :-P

Visited this cocktail bar for one of our weekend lunches. After reaching there we realized it's more than a cocktail bar which offers delicious food along with the drinks.
The ambience is very soothing with minimal interiors and dim lighting (perfect for dates). The restaurant/bar appears to be huge with multiple floors, indoor/outdoor seating arrangements but we couldn't explore since we decided to sit on the first floor.
We were attended by Mr.Abhishek, who was very kind and helped us to figure out the menu and took our order.

A Spinach soup and Paneer tortellini, Asparagus cream cheese Uramiki from sushi bar, A caesar salad along with Tom yum flavoured french fries.
We ordered 2 drinks from the summer special menu(I don't remember the names),but one with mango flavour and another one with pineapple.

The Caesar salad was delicious, the vegetables were fresh and crunchy, The dressing had a perfect consistency and the bread did really complimented the salad, french fries were perfectly fried, good length and nicely spiced.( I can talk only about Caesar Salad and french fries because that's the only thing which I ate)
My friends looked and happy and they appeared to be enjoying their food, Guess the rest of the food was nice too.

The place was really clean and neat, the washroom was well maintained but they can improve the lighting in the washroom for better mirror selfies.

I also noticed that they had this 3 dots symbol on almost everything, we got to know that it featured 3 dots and dash and it's currently in the same place of 3 dots and dash.

Had a great time visiting here.

A versatile and lavishly designed pub, beautifully laid out with strong visual appeal. From the moment I walked in, the concierge experience was smooth and welcoming, setting the tone for the visit.
I was guided straight to a bar top table, where Koina took charge behind the bar. She asked for my preferences and delivered an excellent Old Fashioned cocktail made with whiskey. I also had a Jameson, both of which were well executed. Koina deserves special mention.. confident, attentive, and genuinely engaging. A great presence behind the bar.
The only miss was the boiled peanuts, which were not boiled enough. They were firm rather than soft and soggy, making them difficult to bite and enjoy.
For smokers, the designated area is outside or on the terrace, which is clearly defined and well managed.
A standout moment was being handed Spotify control, being able to play classic rock tracks of my choice added a very personal and memorable touch to the experience.
Overall, a vibrant place with excellent service at the bar and a strong ambience. With minor improvements on food consistency, it delivers a premium pub experience.

Doff Pub is a proper old-school sports pub.

Dropped by for the Chelsea vs Liverpool screening and stayed back for the United game because honestly, this place is built for football lovers.

The beer is preety cheap, a pitcher for around a 1000 bucks. We ended up ordering 4 between 3 of us, helped massively by the cool Bangalore rains, the open seating, and the windy atmosphere.

They have good options in food including and mostly bar bites along with some regional delicacies. We had the Coorgi pork which was lipsmacking — smoky, flavourful, and reason enough to come back again. We also had the crispy chilli mushrooms and green salad.

If you’re someone who believes football is a personality trait, Doff is your kind of place.

Last week, I decided to spend some quality time with myself. I went to Doff Estd. 2011 with a simple plan—to enjoy a beer, sit quietly, and read a good book.
Unfortunately, the experience did not start well. At the entrance, the security guard questioned me in a manner that felt unnecessarily harsh. He repeatedly asked how long I would stay, why I had come, whether I was planning to eat or drink, and seemed quite aggressive in his approach. The interaction left me uncomfortable and created a negative first impression of the place.

Despite that, I chose not to let the experience ruin my evening. Once inside, I found my own corner, ordered a beer, and immersed myself in my book. The atmosphere eventually allowed me to relax and enjoy the solitude I had been seeking. In the end, the day reminded me that while we cannot always control how others treat us, we can choose not to let those moments take away from our peace. What began as an unpleasant experience eventually turned into a meaningful and enjoyable time with myself.

The food was consistently impressive across dishes—especially the sunny side south, goa glow (prawns perfectly cooked and packed with flavor) and the scallion prawn noodles which were super satisfying. Even the smaller plates like the crispy bites and bread were well done and thoughtfully presented.
The cocktails were interesting and well-balanced—definitely worth trying their signatures.
What made it even better was the service—friendly, attentive, and not overbearing. The ambiance is cozy with a nice, slightly upscale vibe, great for a relaxed evening out.
Would definitely come back!

It's a perfect mix of classy cocktails, delicious food and melodic house music. And to top it all off their staff is warm and courteous, always there to make your experience memorable.

They have a pretty interesting line up of Goan inspired cocktails and Asian inspired bar bites which pairs with the cocktails seamlessly.

Go to Mirth with an open mind and let their team take care of your experience for the evening!

text.text:
A foodie whatsapp group I am part of keeps raving about Mirth and so when Brother was visiting, thought we'd skip our usual waterhole on Lavelle and get to Mirth.

We booked a table online and when we walked in, the space was buzzing! The clientele surely looked a bit older, which was heartening too see. The music through the night was awesome and peppy.

We were seated in the balcony section, which is decent, but it is also a smoking zone and at some point we felt a little overwhelmed and got a corner table (right under the loudspeaker!) oh well..we can always win can we.

We ordered a bunch of drinks including a mango manifesto, picante, lavender line, clear intension and food included corn dust, satay street, goa glow and a mushroom stir fry.

All of the food was very good, esp the corn and prawns (goa glow) and satay (chicken)

The drinks were a mixed bag. The Picante was the best..fabulous flavours and mouthfeel, Clear intensions was very good too. The lavender line, had basically 3 sips of booze in the glass, but it was interesting to get the lavender notes in the ample foam the drink came with. Mango Manifesto was terrible and was was wasted after 3 sips (no it didn't get better).

Kushal our wait staff was professional and friendly.

I can see why folks are raving about this place, it is an upscale bar for sure and worth a repeat visit.

text.text:
A small, cozy pub that stands out for its excellent cocktails and exceptional service, making it a pleasant spot for a casual evening.

Drinks – 3.5 / 5
The cocktails are definitely the highlight—well-balanced, flavorful, and with just the right kick. There’s a good variety across different spirits, catering to diverse preferences. While the cocktails are slightly on the pricier side, the regular drinks offer better value for money. The beer selection, however, is quite limited and could benefit from more variety.

Food – 3.5 / 5
The menu leans towards tapas-style dining, offering small plates that allow you to sample multiple dishes. Standout items include the Sunny Side South and Napoli Heatwave Spaghetti, both of which are flavorful and authentic. Introducing a pizza section could further enhance the menu.

Ambience – 2.5 / 5
The space is compact yet cozy, with a mix of high tables, regular seating, and a few larger bench-style tables for groups. However, the limited space can make it feel crowded, with noise levels rising quickly and movement becoming slightly inconvenient. The outdoor seating area with a designated smoking zone offers a welcome escape. The dim lighting sets a relaxed mood, and the table lamps add a thoughtful touch.

Service – 5 / 5
Service is the standout feature of this pub. The staff are warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. A special mention to Kushal, whose excellent recommendations and friendly demeanor significantly enhanced the overall experience.

Despite a few limitations in space and menu variety, this place is worth visiting for its cocktails and outstanding service. It’s an ideal spot if you’re looking to unwind with good drinks and great hospitality.

Overall rating: 3.5/5

text.text:
I recently visited DAYSIE during their Weekends in Thailand experience, where they showcase global flavours region by region and it’s so much more than just Thai green curry. I tried dishes I’d never had before, and I was super excited with every plate that arrived.

We began with their amazing drinks, which set the tone for the meal. The grilled cottage cheese was smoky, tender and packed with flavour. The Thai lemongrass chicken was fresh, aromatic and perfectly balanced. The Bangkok street BBQ jumbo prawns were juicy and beautifully charred, while the jungle basil stir fry brought bold, herbaceous flavours that really stood out. The Khao Man Gai Reloaded was comforting yet refined, showing off so much technique in a familiar dish.

We ended with the Sago Ma-Muang — lush mango and silky sago that made for the perfect cooling finish after such a flavour-packed experience.

What really added a personal touch was the involvement of the owner himself, who checked in on us both while we were being seated and again during dessert to ensure we were comfortable and enjoying our meal. That level of attention is always appreciated and reflects a strong focus on customer satisfaction.

We began our meal with veg dumplings, which were absolutely delicious — perfectly steamed, well-seasoned, and packed with flavor. I also ordered a Diet Coke and a tofu-based starter, which was equally satisfying with a nice balance of spices and textures. For the main course, I tried their pizza, which was well-made with a crisp crust and generous toppings. The Pad Thai, however, was just average — lacking a bit of the authentic tangy-sweet balance I was expecting. We wrapped up the meal with Baked Alaska for dessert, which was decent, though not particularly memorable.

While the food and service were impressive, I do feel that the ambience could use a little upgrade. The interiors were functional but didn’t quite match the warmth and attentiveness of the staff. With a bit of improvement in the overall setting, Tycoons has great potential to be a favorite go-to in Indiranagar. I’d definitely consider going back, especially for the hospitality and some of those tasty appetizers.

We started with the sun-dried tomato garlic bread and eggplant bruschetta, and both were flavourful and nicely done. For mains, we tried the spicy veg pizza — and it was definitely super spicy, just the way the name promises, so spice lovers will enjoy it.

The mocktails were refreshing — we tried a cranberry juice–based one and a creamy mango-flavoured drink, both were well balanced and enjoyable.

Overall, a beautiful place with great food, attentive service, and a relaxed dining experience. Definitely worth visiting in Indiranagar.

I had reserved a table for lunch with a friend, hoping to enjoy good food and a pleasant afternoon. We started with a couple of drinks, and since my friend wanted hers sweeter, we requested an adjustment. That part was handled well.

Next, we ordered a starter after reading the description of Tartar di Tonno:
“A refined tuna tartare, infused with the subtle heat of ginger, accompanied by a vibrant passion fruit coulis and a velvety cheese cream (fish).”

We had no idea what the dish was supposed to look like, but when it arrived, we were completely shocked. The plate had chopped, cold pieces of tuna that looked nothing like what was described—it genuinely resembled cat food. We couldn’t even bring ourselves to take a bite.

We immediately asked if they could take the dish back. Instead of cancelling it, the staff told us they would “toss and cook it,” but even then, the dish was neither refunded nor replaced. The waiter never warned us that it was a raw-fish preparation, and the menu description did not make this clear either. For a dish priced at ₹900, this was extremely disappointing.

What made it worse was that instead of preparing something new, they simply baked the same dish and returned it. It looked exactly the same, and when we finally tasted it, it smelled unpleasant. We asked to have it packed just to end the ordeal. The entire lunch was ruined, and my friend even experienced itchiness in her mouth after tasting it.

We settled the bill and left, thoroughly disappointed. I would never return and definitely would not recommend this place to anyone. You’re better off going to Chianti, where the food is far better, reasonably priced, and the customer service is excellent.

Had a wonderful experience here! The ambience is fantastic, making it a perfect place to hang out with friends and family. We visited on a weekday afternoon and were able to get a table without a reservation, though I hear weekends can get quite busy.

The brewery offers a great selection of freshly brewed beers, and the beer tasting platter is a fantastic option if you want to sample multiple varieties. While I'm no beer expert, I genuinely enjoyed every beer I tried.

The food was the real highlight of the visit. The Chilli Billy Pork was incredibly tender and flavorful, with the fat practically melting in the mouth. The Pepperoni Pizza and Mixed Pork Pizza were excellent, featuring a thin crust and generous toppings. The BBQ Lamb Chops had a lovely smoky flavor, while the Butter Garlic Prawns and Honey Glazed Chicken Wings were equally delicious.

The drinks were refreshing, and the Pull Me Up Tiramisu was the perfect way to end the meal—light, creamy, and absolutely heavenly.

The presentation of every dish was impressive, and the quality matched the looks. The prices are on the higher side, but the overall experience, food quality, drinks, and ambience make it worth a visit.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for great food, craft beer, and a lively atmosphere in Bangalore! 🍺🍕🍖✨

⭐ 4.5/5

Visited Chianti in Indiranagar for lunch around 1:30 PM and had a great overall experience.

We started with a bruschetta—crispy toasted baguette topped with tomatoes, garlic, olive oil, and parmesan. Simple and well done, though slightly on the crispier side. For drinks, we ordered a peach iced tea, a virgin mojito, and a virgin sangria with fresh fruit pieces—it was refreshing and nicely balanced.

For mains, the bruschetta pizza with sun-dried tomatoes was excellent—flavourful and satisfying, though a bit heavy after starters. The highlight was the ravioli di spinaci e ricotta (homemade ravioli with spinach and ricotta), served in a buttery garlic sauce with hints of tomato—rich, creamy, and absolutely delicious. Best shared, as it can feel slightly heavy for one person.

We ended with tiramisu, which was light, soft, and very enjoyable—slightly on the sweeter side but well balanced.

A special mention to our server, Amarjeet, who was extremely helpful with recommendations and ensured smooth service throughout.

The total bill came to around ₹3,000 for three, which felt reasonable for the quality and experience. Overall, a very good meal—definitely a place I’d visit again and recommend.

text.text:
Chianti continues to be one of the best places in Bangalore for authentic Italian food, and this meal was a reminder of why it has such a loyal following.

We started with the Suppli al Pomodoro, which was perfectly crisp on the outside and packed with flavour inside, followed by the DIY Bruschetta that was fresh, vibrant, and fun to customize. We also tried the Chicken Ravioli, which was comforting, well-balanced, and beautifully executed. Another standout was the Doppio Ravioli, part of Chianti’s Monthly Pasta Special, where they showcase lesser-known handmade pasta shapes from Italy. This unique pasta parcel featured two different fillings in a single bite, making it one of the most memorable dishes of the meal.

For dessert, the Mango Crostata was light and refreshing with just the right amount of sweetness, while the classic Tiramisu was rich, creamy, and the perfect way to end the meal.

From the food to the service and ambience, Chianti continues to deliver a consistently authentic Italian dining experience that’s worth coming back for.

I recently visited AnTeRa Kitchen and Bar in Indiranagar, and it turned out to be an absolutely delightful experience. From the moment we walked in, the ambience struck me as breathtaking and mesmerising. The space beautifully combines a simple Indian aesthetic with subtle Western design elements, creating a warm yet classy atmosphere that makes you want to linger.

What truly stood out, however, was the food. The menu reflects a thoughtful blend of North Indian authenticity with a refined touch of South Indian culinary style. Each dish felt carefully crafted, maintaining traditional flavours while elevating them with a contemporary presentation. The balance between richness and subtlety was impressive.

A special mention must go to the Paneer Chatpata—it was bursting with flavour, perfectly spiced, and incredibly satisfying. The Kaju Chicken was equally remarkable, rich, crispy and absolutely delicious. Both dishes are a must-try for anyone visiting.

The service added significantly to the overall experience. The staff were extremely attentive and courteous, constantly checking in on us and ensuring that we were comfortable. What I particularly appreciated was their proactive approach—they made sure we didn’t have to serve ourselves, which added a touch of luxury to the meal.

Overall, AnTeRa Kitchen and Bar offers not just great food, but a complete dining experience. With its stunning ambience, thoughtfully curated menu, and exceptional service, it is definitely a place I would recommend and revisit.

text.text:
A Royal South Indian Escape with a Chinese Twist!
I recently dropped by this popular spot during a visit to Indiranagar. Though it's a massive three-story resto-bar known for dinner, I stopped in for lunch, and wow—the ambiance immediately transports you straight to a remote, charming village in Andhra Pradesh or Telangana. The decor is steeped in rich Indian heritage; honestly, walking up the staircase made me feel like I was checking into a king’s palace!
The place is top-notch when it comes to hygiene, which is always a massive plus. While they have an extensive Indian menu, I veered off-road and ordered Chinese—the noodles and chicken drumsticks were absolutely on point. The staff were incredibly friendly and took the time to guide me through the menu. My only regret? I didn't have enough stomach space left for their famous biryani. I'll just have to call that "unfinished business" for my next visit.

Bonus: Valet parking is available, so zero parking headaches in busy Indiranagar. Highly recommended!

Yesterday, on 25th December, four of us went to this club and paid ₹1000 per person for entry. Before going in, we asked if one person could just check the crowd inside, but the staff didn’t allow that. Instead, they showed us videos and music clips, saying the crowd inside was really good. Based on that, we decided to enter.
But once we were inside, everything was totally different. There was hardly any crowd, and the sound quality was very bad. Since we had already paid the entry fee, we couldn’t leave and had no choice. Honestly, it felt like we wasted our entire Christmas day here.
Then we had to struggle to get a table. After waiting for around 30–35 minutes, we finally got a table in a corner upstairs. We ordered food and beer, vodka’s but the food quality was really poor not even enjoyable.
Later, when we went to the dance floor, we were shocked to see bouncers separating boys and girls. I have never seen this kind of behaviour in any club or pub before. We are from Delhi and know how to party and behave in a crowd, but this place felt more like a school where you’re told not to talk to girls.
It honestly felt like the club thinks it runs only because of girls, which is not true. Clubs run because people pay for entry, especially stag entries.
Overall, a very disappointing experience. I would not recommend this place if you want to enjoy your weekend or celebrate a special day.

text.text:
There is a specific kind of magic found in a pub that doesn't try too hard. Murphy’s Brew is exactly that—a masterclass in understated Irish hospitality. While many establishments lean into the loud, caricatured version of Emerald Isle culture, Murphy’s opts for an authentic, grounded atmosphere that feels more like a local haunt in Cork than a tourist trap.
The prose of the evening is written in the pour. Their stout is exceptional, boasting a creamy, persistent head and a flavor profile that hits that perfect, bittersweet equilibrium. It is served with the kind of practiced precision that suggests the staff view bartending as a craft rather than a chore. Speaking of the service, it is attentive without being intrusive, a rare find definitely!

Visiting on a Saturday offers a surprisingly serene experience. Instead of the usual weekend chaos, you’ll find a mellow, conversational hum that allows the character of the wood and the warmth of the lighting to take center stage. The food serves as a reliable, comforting companion to the drink. It was decent, hearty, and honest. If you appreciate a place where the quality of the pint matches the quiet dignity of the surroundings, Murphy’s Brew is your next destination.

Came here for Lunch with Family and overall it was a wonderful experience.

This was our first time time but had heard about Iron Hill from a lot of friends so it was time to actually experience all the stories I had heard and happy to say my experience was goood too.

Let’s start with the Google Maps location, if you are coming from the Old Airport side the Google Maps might show you the way towards the backside which is the exit gate. Slightly difficult to navigate during peak hours. The main entrance is on the Marathalli main road near the Innovative Multiplex.

They have Vallet parking available so parking the car was easy and trouble free.

Since we had kids in our group the selection for seating was limited. During the weekends kids are allowed inside so the view might not be open. We actually prefer the inner space so it was good for us.

Coming to the food it was easy to order and they have the menu integrated with Swiggy Dining which was something I was seeing for the first time. The software was well integrated.

Coming to the food tried a lot of things, The Mini Burgers Non Veg and fish fingers were definitely a stand out though all the food tasted good. Normally I don’t expect brewery food to taste good but this was a surprise here.

Coming to the drinks we tried the sampler and a few mocktails and it was all good.SincityCider Beer recommended if you want to try a really sweeet beer.

Also thanks to Aryan and all the service people. They were easy to talk to and answered all our doubts and were easily visible on the floor at most times though there were a few instances I did have to search but that’s ok.

The ambiance is good and a lot of places inside to take pictures and a few games too if you want to play mostly good for the kids.

Overall it was a good experience and would recommend people to come here.

One unique think I noticed is looks like they have some tie up with Udrive which was written on the vallet slip so incase you do unplanned drinking I think you would be able to get a driver here soon to drive your car since I had seen reviews where people had told me during nights there are cops close to the entrance so be cautious about that.

Located inside a mall with convenient basement parking. There are two lifts—one goes directly to the 4th floor, while the other takes you to the 3rd floor, from where you can use the escalator. The brewery is on the 4th floor. As soon as you step in, the place feels quite spacious. The ambience is pleasant, especially the pots placed along the roof, which add a nice touch.

We were a group of 25 and they comfortably accommodated us. Even smaller groups or couples will easily find seating. They offer happy hour deals like 1+1 on drinks or a 15% discount with pre-booking.
Their most popular brew is the Mango Beer. We ordered five pitchers. Honestly, it tastes more like beer mixed with Maaza—very unique and refreshing. Loved it. They also have other craft beer options available.
The crowd felt more suited to boomers; we didn’t really notice a younger crowd. Music is played via USB, and the staff wasn’t flexible about changing it. While we were there, they played slow 90s English tracks. Even though we wanted something upbeat to dance to, the music remained unchanged, which kind of dampened the vibe.
Food was just okay. We tried most of the starters; the mushroom starter stood out and was quite popular. The restroom is located outside the restaurant and felt a bit old.
Overall, it’s a decent place to relax and spend some time.

⭐ Review: Toit Mahadevapura – Mahadevapura, Bangalore
If you’re looking for one of the best places to unwind after the office in Mahadevapura, Toit is easily top of the list. This lively brewpub has earned strong praise from locals and visitors alike for its vibrant atmosphere, great craft beers, and solid food options, making it a go-to hangout for colleagues, friends, and anyone who wants a relaxed yet fun night out.
🍺 Vibe & Ambience — The space is spacious and stylish, with a mix of indoor and outdoor seating that’s perfect for winding down after work. The industrial-chic interiors with exposed brick and cozy lighting set a welcoming tone, and many reviewers loved the relaxed, social feel — great for chatting over drinks without blasting music drowning out conversation.
🍻 Drinks & Brews — Toit’s craft beers are a highlight, with a good variety of house brews on tap that pair beautifully with their food. Many patrons specifically recommend trying the Belgian Dark Ale and Red Ale, and the overall beer selection is one of the main reasons people keep coming back.
🍕 Food & Pairings — While the focus is on beer, the food here gets strong marks too. Classic pub fare like pizzas, nachos, ribs, and prawns are frequently mentioned as crowd-pleasers, and desserts like tiramisu or cheesecake earn special shout-outs from diners.
👩‍💼 Service & Crowd — Many reviews mention attentive, friendly staff that elevate the experience. Weeknights are especially enjoyable, with more space and quicker service, though weekends can get busy — reservations are recommended if you’re heading there after work.
💸 Who It’s For — With reasonable prices and a lively yet relaxed environment, Toit is ideal for after-work drinks with colleagues, casual meetups with friends, or even a low-key date night.
Bottom Line: Toit Mahadevapura is one of the places to visit in Mahadevapura after office hours — great beers, good food, and a vibe that hits the sweet spot between laid-back and lively.

Had a blasting experience at TOIT. The crispy calamari was outstanding. The best I have ever had. Definitely gonna come back to some more calamari. Desserts and the Mushroom Lamb Pasta with White Sauce was pretty good. Fish and chips were average. Mocktails are below average in taste. Overall experience is quite good.

Here's a more elaborate and polished review:

Had an absolutely fantastic experience at Toit. The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the Crispy Calamari—it was hands down the best calamari I’ve ever had. Perfectly crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and packed with flavor. It's one of those dishes that keeps you thinking about it long after the meal is over, and I’ll definitely be coming back just to have it again.

The Mushroom Lamb Pasta in White Sauce was another standout dish. The pasta was cooked well, the sauce was rich and creamy without being overwhelming, and the combination of mushrooms and lamb worked beautifully together. The desserts were also quite enjoyable and provided a satisfying finish to the meal.

The Fish and Chips, however, were fairly average and didn’t leave a lasting impression compared to some of the other dishes on the menu. Similarly, the mocktails were a bit disappointing. While they looked appealing, the flavors felt underwhelming and lacked the punch one would expect.

That said, the overall experience was very positive. The lively atmosphere, great food options, and excellent signature dishes more than made up for a few misses. If you're visiting TOIT, the Crispy Calamari is an absolute must-try. Looking forward to returning and exploring more of the menu—though another plate of that amazing calamari is definitely going to be my first order! ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆

text.text:
Arbor brewing company is an old brewpub  in Bengaluru,close to CBD but devoid of excess noise, excessive crowd and hustle bustle, having its own relaxed ambience.Not too crowded and a warm English style  ambience.
Located on the 3rd Floor, opp to Garuda Mall, it is well within reach of central Bengaluru.
Craft beer is good ,starters and main course are equally good and tasty.
Old School Chilly chicken ,Salt and pepper prawn,mutton chapli kababs are made really well.
Bangalore bliss is  a smooth and light beer whereas their signature Smooth Criminal is actually a potent and dangerous criminal, smooth to taste but hits all of a sudden.Beware of this.
Courteous service with a foosball table, not too jarring music and a lively vibe.
Valet parking available.
Prices are steep though and the bouncer at the entrance,regularly  moving around the tables in the pub all the while is an unwelcome move.

text.text:
Visited ShakesBierre Brewpub & Kitchen during their Oktoberfest celebration and honestly, it felt like a mini beer festival right in the middle of Bangalore. The whole place had proper festive vibes — blue-white décor, themed menu, lively music, and that classic clinking-glasses energy you expect from Oktoberfest.

The craft beers were easily the highlight. Fresh brews on tap, smooth lagers, wheat beers, and some really fun seasonal specials that paired beautifully with the food. Loved how the menu actually suggested beer pairings for each dish — made the experience feel curated rather than random ordering.

Food was solid pub-style comfort. The grilled meats and kebabs were juicy, portions were generous, and everything went perfectly with the beers. It’s the kind of place where you come hungry and leave happy. Service was friendly and quick even though it was packed, and the staff helped with recommendations.

Ambience-wise, it’s spacious, energetic, and perfect for groups — rooftop/indoor seating, music, and a proper party atmosphere without feeling chaotic.

If you’re looking for an Oktoberfest-style night out with great brews, good food, and fun vibes, this is definitely one of the best spots in the city. Would happily come back for every beer festival they host. 🍺✨

text.text:
Stories used to be one of those well-known Bangalore brewery spots that people genuinely recommended, especially for its pizzas and garlic cheese breads. But now, the place feels a bit under-maintained and inconsistent, and a lot of that old charm seems missing.

The ambience is still decent, but since much of the seating is open-air, it can get quite sunny and windy during summer afternoons, which affects the overall comfort.

Coming to the food

* The pizzas and sourdough-based dishes were disappointing, with the dough itself tasting pretty average and poorly done compared to how the place used to be.
* The garlic cheese bread, which was once a highlight, now also feels just okay.
* Other dishes like pastas and starters are very inconsistent—some are decent while others completely miss the mark.
* The mango sticky rice dessert didn’t work at all personally and felt underwhelming.

The drinks are probably the strongest part of the experience now. The piña colada, refreshers, and milkshakes were all pretty decent, but not enough to compensate for the disappointing food.

Portion sizes also feel slightly small for the pricing, making the place feel expensive for what it currently offers.

Ironically, the food we eventually ordered was actually quite good, which is the only reason this review gets an extra star. Otherwise, based on the overall experience, it would have been a 1-star rating from us.

A brewery should be judged by what it consistently offers, not by what it doesn't have on a particular day. If key menu items and popular beer options are unavailable, it significantly impacts the experience.

Perhaps it was just an unfortunate day to visit. But as a customer, that's not really my problem. Unfortunately, the overall experience wasn't compelling enough to make us want to return, and it's not a place we'd consider for a second visit.

text.text:
We were seated at a corner table on the rooftop. It's very chilly and windy up there. Nice ambience. Rooftop seating appears to be a fairly popular choice among patrons.

The tables and bar chairs are quite dusty due to the wind, traffic and air which should be fine except that the staff do not clean the tables before diners are seated.

They have different types of seating available high, low,  indoor, outdoor, etc.
They have put in  quite a bit of effort into keeping the ambience of the pub relaxing as well as comfortably bright with their decorative lights and interior decoration.

The menu contains a fairly large number of dishes and drinks to pick from.

The Calcutta chicken cutlets were
not awful however they were definitely
drier than raw rice.

The pork coorgi was very flavourful. It had less fat which is great and a good serving of meat.

The curry leaf prawns we had were amazing as  they were large pieces for one and additionally because the presentation was unique.  The prawns were juicy, fresh and the taste was delish.

We also had beer battered onion rings and apple pie with ice cream amongst more.

The sizzling brownie is awesome you may  burn your teeth and tongue even .... despite the  biting cold weather. It was gooey, had a well sized scoop of ice cream and was definitely the highlight of my dinner.

For desserts I would give them an overall 4.8 out of 5.
As for food I will probably give a 4 out of 5.

Staff are polite and friendly but service is very slow. The staff attending on us forgot one of our orders and double billed us on another item.  When pointed out the staff were quick to rectify the error. The restaurant has several staff but they seem to be quite busy for the most part.

Visited Misosexy recently and had a good experience overall. The ambiance is stylish and enjoyable, though the music was a bit too loud and the AC felt quite strong.

Food-wise, there were some real highlights. The Shanghai soup dumplings had a delicious, flavorful broth inside, although the dumpling wrapper was slightly thicker than I prefer. The smoked sauce chicken dumplings were excellent and definitely a must-try. I also loved the Prawn Tempura Uramaki Sushi—fresh, well-balanced, and very tasty.

The ramen was average compared to the other dishes, but the appetizers and sushi made up for it. Worth visiting for the vibe and some standout dishes! 🍜🥟🍣

text.text:
I recently visited Misosexy in Bangalore and had a really enjoyable dining experience. The ambience is stylish yet relaxed, with a modern, slightly playful vibe that lives up to the restaurant’s name. The lighting, music, and seating all make it a great spot for a casual dinner or a fun night out with friends.
We started with a few dumplings, which were delicate, well‑wrapped, and packed with flavour—the filling was juicy and properly seasoned, and the outer wrappers were soft with just the right bite. The pork spare ribs were a highlight: tender on the inside, slightly caramelised on the outside, and glazed with a balanced sweet‑and‑savory sauce that wasn’t too heavy.
The prawn tempura uramaki sushi was fresh and satisfying; the prawns were crisp from the tempura coating, and the rice and nori wrapped everything together nicely. The roll was neither too dry nor too oily, and it felt like a good fusion of Japanese technique and contemporary plating.
We also ordered a couple of mocktails, both of which were refreshing, well‑balanced, and visually appealing. The bartender clearly paid attention to presentation and flavour, avoiding overly sugary or artificial tastes.
Overall, Misosexy Bangalore impressed me with its creative menu, consistent execution, and cool atmosphere. If you’re in the mood for Asian‑inspired small plates, good sushi, and stylish drinks, I’d definitely recommend trying it.

text.text: Having passed by this place numerous times, finally got the chance of visiting the place. This place didn't disappoint and might be the best brewery in Whitefield. The ambiance is really great with great interiors and a huge seating capacity. Its outside seating is different from the inner seating area and is just as good. The service is pretty good as well. Items came fairly quickly and the staff was attentive and friendly. Coming to the food, the presentation and preparation was on point with all the dishes looking and tasting great. Prices are comparable to other breweries so that way I felt this was more value for money than others. Their beers were also good and they have a good variety in tap. Ample parking space and a good place to hangout with friends and family. Definitely worth recommending and revisiting again👌

Visited Oasis Brewery, Whitefield recently for their Summer Collective, and it turned out to be a refreshing experience beyond just food and drinks.

The space has a great balance of lively brewery vibes and a relaxed atmosphere, making it ideal for catching up with friends or planning a unique date. What stood out was how thoughtfully the Summer Collective activities were curated — from interactive experiences to entertainment that kept the evening engaging without feeling overwhelming.

The food paired well with their drinks, and the ambience transitions beautifully from a laid-back afternoon setting to a vibrant evening scene. If you're someone who enjoys places that offer more than just dining, Oasis is definitely worth exploring.

A great spot in Whitefield for good conversations, drinks, and memorable experiences.

text.text:
I recently visited a beautiful pet-friendly restaurant and had such an amazing experience that I couldn’t wait to share it. The food was absolutely awesome, and every dish we ordered was full of flavor and perfectly prepared. If you ever visit this place, Pizza and Nachos are a must-try. The pizza was cheesy, fresh, and loaded with toppings, while the nachos were crispy and served with delicious dips that made them even better.
One of the best things about this restaurant is its peaceful and refreshing ambience. The place is surrounded by lots of greenery, which creates a calm and relaxing atmosphere. There is also a lovely fountain that adds to the beauty of the space and makes it perfect for spending quality time with friends and family. Another highlight is that it is a pet-friendly restaurant, so you can happily take your furry friend along and enjoy the outing together. Watching pets enjoy the open space made the experience even more cheerful.
The mocktails were equally impressive and very refreshing. They were beautifully presented and tasted amazing. Overall, this restaurant offers great food, a wonderful ambience, and a memorable dining experience that I would definitely recommend to everyone.
